# @vestra-player/sdk 1.5.13: full reference

> Everything needed to write a Vestra Player plugin (plugin API `vestra/1`): the guides, every public declaration of `@vestra-player/sdk` and `@vestra-player/sdk/testing` with its documentation, and the complete source of the example plugins. Generated from the SDK's sources by scripts/llms.mjs; the short index is llms.txt.

How to read this file: the declarations are TypeScript declaration files whose doc comments keep only the description and the tags @capability (the manifest capability a call needs), @player (the oldest player version), @param, @returns, @throws (`code` (throws | rejects) condition) and @deprecated. Examples and longer remarks are in the documentation site and in node_modules/@vestra-player/sdk/dist/**/*.d.ts. Only what is declared here exists; do not use other members.

Limits: 160 commands per plugin and 1024 in the player (`limit`); menu ids for the first path segment: `@open`, `@playback`, `@subtitles`, `@video`, `@audio`, `@screen`, `@settings`; manifest: id ≤ 128 bytes, name, author ≤ 64 characters, punchline ≤ 120, description ≤ 2000, tags ≤ 8 of ≤ 24 characters, license ≤ 64, sourceUrl ≤ 2048 bytes, icon PNG or JPEG ≤ 512 KB and 1024 px per side, readme, changelog ≤ 256 KB.

## Tutorial: Getting started

This guide walks through a complete Vestra Player plugin: the files it is made of, the manifest, a first command, a window, tests, and packaging. The API reference is split into @vestra-player/sdk (the plugin API) and @vestra-player/sdk/testing (the test host); start from Plugin and Scope.

### How plugins run

- Each plugin runs in its own Node.js process (Node.js 26, which the player ships) started by the player. It can use the Node standard library, the file system, the network and npm packages.
- The player loads the entry module and calls its **default export** `activate(plugin)`. The `plugin` object is created by the player; the plugin imports the SDK **as types only**, so a built plugin contains nothing but its own code.
- Everything a plugin creates (commands, windows, panels, filters, listeners…) is a handle owned by `plugin` or a child scope, and is released automatically when the plugin stops. There is no cleanup function to return.
- Plugins are trusted code. Manifest capabilities are a contract that the player enforces per call (a missing one fails with `code: "capability"`), not a security sandbox.
- The API is the same on macOS and Windows. A feature a system cannot provide fails with `unsupported`; each method documents its platform differences.

### Rules for plugins

Every plugin, in the official plugin repository or not, follows these rules. They keep plugins independent of each other and portable.

- **Only the public SDK.** Import `@vestra-player/sdk` with `import type` only (a runtime import fails `vestra-plugin build`) and `@vestra-player/sdk/testing` only in tests. `@vestra-player/sdk/runtime` and the SDK's internal modules are for the player.
- **No other plugins.** Do not import another plugin's code, read its directory or data directory, or talk to it privately (shared files, sockets, messages). A plugin must load, run and stop while no other plugin is installed. Plugins share only what the API makes public: player state, timeline marks, menus, settings pages.
- **No system commands.** Do not run `open`, `sips`, `plutil`, `security`, `cmd`, `powershell` or similar. Use the API (`plugin.system` to open files and links, `plugin.clipboard`, `plugin.secrets`, `plugin.tools` for ffmpeg and ffprobe) or portable Node.js code. If the API lacks something every system needs, ask for it in the SDK repository.
- **macOS and Windows.** The same code runs on both: build paths with `node:path`, write package paths with `/`, and handle `unsupported` where a method documents a platform difference.
- **Your own id.** `<owner>.<name>`, where the owner is your GitHub user or organization. `vestra` and `vestra.*` are reserved for the plugins built into the player.

### Install

```sh
mkdir my-plugin && cd my-plugin
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm i -D @vestra-player/sdk
```

The package brings its own TypeScript 5.x and `@types/node`, and the `vestra-plugin` command line tool.

### Files

```text
my-plugin/
  manifest.json        identity and capabilities
  main.ts              the entry module
  ui/hello.slint       optional: user interface
  tests/main.test.ts   tests (node:test)
  package.json         dev dependency and scripts
```

`package.json` scripts:

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "check": "vestra-plugin check",
    "test": "vestra-plugin test",
    "build": "vestra-plugin build",
    "pack": "vestra-plugin pack"
  },
  "devDependencies": { "@vestra-player/sdk": "^1.5.0" }
}
```

### The manifest

```json
{
  "id": "me.hello",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.osd", "playback.read", "events"]
}
```

| Field              | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`               | Non-empty, globally unique identifier; use `author.plugin`.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `version`          | Three non-negative integers `x.y.z`. `vestra-plugin build` writes it into `dist/manifest.json`.                                                                                                              |
| `apiVersion`       | Always `"vestra/1"` for this major version of the SDK.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `entry`            | Relative path inside the package: `.ts` during development, `.js` after building.                                                                                                                            |
| `capabilities`     | Only names from the table below.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `minPlayerVersion` | Optional `x.y.z`: the oldest player that can load the plugin. Older players refuse it with `versionMismatch` ("requires Vestra Player ≥ x.y.z"). Set it when you use API added after SDK 1.0 (see Versions). |

Optional display fields (player 0.2.0), shown by the plugin store and plugin manager:

| Field         | Rule                                                                                          |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | 1–64 characters, one line.                                                                    |
| `author`      | 1–64 characters, one line.                                                                    |
| `punchline`   | One-line summary, 1–120 characters.                                                           |
| `description` | Plain text, 1–2000 characters; line breaks allowed.                                           |
| `tags`        | Up to 8 tags, 1–24 characters each, unique ignoring case.                                     |
| `icon`        | Package path of a PNG or JPEG, at most 512 KB and 1024 pixels per side (256×256 recommended). |
| `readme`      | Package path of a UTF-8 `.md` file (≤ 256 KB). Default: `README.md` when present.             |
| `changelog`   | Same, default `CHANGELOG.md` when present.                                                    |
| `sourceUrl`   | `https:` address of the source code.                                                          |
| `license`     | 1–64 characters, preferably an SPDX expression such as `MIT`.                                 |

A manifest with every field. `id`, `apiVersion`, `entry` and `capabilities` are required; without `version`, `vestra-plugin build` takes it from `--version` or `package.json`.

```json
{
  "id": "me.hello",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.osd"],
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.4.1",
  "name": "Hello",
  "author": "Me",
  "punchline": "Says hello from the Tools menu.",
  "description": "A first plugin.\nIt adds Tools ▸ Hello, which shows an on-screen message.",
  "tags": ["example"],
  "icon": "assets/icon.png",
  "readme": "README.md",
  "changelog": "CHANGELOG.md",
  "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/me/hello",
  "license": "MIT"
}
```

Unknown fields, unknown capabilities and paths that leave the package directory (including through symbolic links) are rejected. The id's characters are ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`; the official plugin repository additionally requires `<GitHub user or organization>.<plugin name>`. The `vestra.` prefix (and the id `vestra`, in any case) is reserved for the plugins built into the player: from player 0.4.1 the player refuses to install such a package (`reserved`). Every other plugin is a third-party plugin, including those hosted in the official repository.

| Capability                             | Opens                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `commands`                             | `commands.add`, `host.run`                                                                              |
| `ui.window`                            | `windows.create`                                                                                        |
| `ui.mount`                             | `panels.mount`, `panels.bottom` / `.sidebar` / `.backdrop`                                              |
| `ui.dialog`                            | `dialogs.*`                                                                                             |
| `ui.osd`                               | `osd.show`, `osd.panel`                                                                                 |
| `ui.drop`                              | `drops.provide`, `Panel.onDrop`                                                                         |
| `ui.theme`                             | `appearance.set`                                                                                        |
| `ui.settings`                          | `settings.page`, `settings.show`                                                                        |
| `playback.read`                        | reading `player.state` at start, `refresh`, `stats`, `chapters`, `audioDevices`, `timeline.marks`       |
| `events`                               | live `player.state` / `onChange`, panel visibility, subtitle and window updates                         |
| `playback.control`                     | `player.open`, `setPaused`, `seek`, `setRate`, … and `power.preventSleep`                               |
| `producer.av`                          | `player.openStream` (with `playback.control`: the stream becomes the player's source)                   |
| `processing.video`                     | `video.filter` (with `playback.read` and `events`), `video.view`, `video.render` (with `playback.read`) |
| `processing.audio`                     | `audio.filter` (with `playback.read` and `events`)                                                      |
| `subtitles.read` / `subtitles.control` | reading / changing subtitles                                                                            |
| `media.read` / `media.control`         | `media.capture`, snapshot exports                                                                       |
| `source.resolve`                       | `resolvers.add`                                                                                         |
| `plugins.manage`                       | `packages.validate`, `rollback`, `setEnabled`, `uninstall`                                              |
| `clipboard`                            | `clipboard.*`                                                                                           |
| `window.control`                       | `window.setVideoArea`, `setAlwaysOnTop`, `setCursorAutoHide`, `setPictureInPicture`                     |
| `bindings.manage`                      | `bindings.*`                                                                                            |
| `timeline.marks`                       | `timeline.layer()`                                                                                      |
| `secrets`                              | `secrets.*`                                                                                             |

No capability is needed for `tools`, `storage`, `system`, `ui.image`, `plugin.app`, reading `window.state` and `appearance.theme`, and `packages.list`.

### A first plugin

```ts
// main.ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "where",
    path: ["Tools", "Where am I?"],
    bindings: ["Ctrl+Alt+W"],
    enabled: () => plugin.player.state.phase === "ready",
    run: () => {
      const { position, duration } = plugin.player.state;
      return plugin.osd.show(
        `${position?.toFixed(1)} s of ${duration?.toFixed(1)} s`,
      );
    },
  });
}
```

- `path` is the menu path, matched by exact titles. "Tools" is a new top-level menu of this plugin. To put an item into one of the player's own menus, start the path with its id instead of its title, which depends on the player's language: `["@video", "Blur"]` (also `@open`, `@playback`, `@subtitles`, `@audio`, `@screen`, `@settings`; player 0.3.0).
- `enabled` is a function: the SDK re-evaluates it after every handler and every state change it receives, and sends only changes. This needs `events` to follow outside changes.
- `run` may return a promise. Errors thrown or rejected there go to `plugin.onError`, then to the plugin log.
- Commands are registered in the background; activation succeeds once every registration made during `activate` succeeded.

### A window

User interfaces are Slint files in the package. The plugin writes properties and handles callbacks; property and callback names may be written in camelCase and are converted to Slint's kebab-case.

```slint
// ui/hello.slint
import { Button } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";

export component Hello inherits Window {
    title: "Hello";
    in property <string> message;
    in property <bool> can-seek;
    callback jump(float);
    background: Theme.bg-panel;
    VerticalLayout {
        Text { text: root.message; color: Theme.text; }
        Button { text: "Back 10 s"; enabled: root.can-seek; clicked => { root.jump(-10); } }
    }
}
```

```ts
const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/hello.slint");
window.bind(() => ({
  message: plugin.player.state.source ?? "Nothing is playing",
  canSeek: plugin.player.state.can.seek,
}));
window.on("jump", (delta: number) =>
  plugin.player.seek(Math.max(0, (plugin.player.state.position ?? 0) + delta)),
);
plugin.commands.add({
  id: "hello",
  path: ["Tools", "Hello…"],
  run: () => window.show(),
});
```

This needs `ui.window`, `commands`, `playback.read`, `events` and `playback.control`. Bind callbacks before the first `show()`.

`@vestra/theme.slint` and `@vestra/widgets.slint` come from the player at run time. For editor support, point the Slint language server's library path `vestra` at `node_modules/@vestra-player/sdk/slint/vestra` (a read-only copy that matches the player).

### Testing

`@vestra-player/sdk/testing` runs a plugin against `TestHost`, an in-memory player that speaks the real protocol, so the SDK's own logic runs unchanged. There is no decoding, Slint or native window.

```ts
// tests/main.test.ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("shows the position", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url), // reads manifest.json
  });
  host.setSource({ phase: "ready", position: 12, duration: 60 });
  await host.settle();
  await host.command("where").run();
  assert.deepEqual(host.osd, ["12.0 s of 60.0 s"]);
  await stop();
});
```

Useful controls: `host.command(id).run()`, `host.press("Ctrl+Alt+W")`, `host.window(id).emit(callback, ...args)` and `.props`, `host.openElsewhere(path)`, `host.handle(method, fn)` to inject failures (throw a `HostError`), `host.settle()` to wait until the plugin's host calls are answered (it does not wait for the plugin's own file reads or child processes: poll the result you assert on, see `settle`). See TestHost.

Run them with `npm test` (`vestra-plugin test`, which is `node --test tests/*.test.{ts,mjs}`).

### Check, run, build and pack

```text
vestra-plugin check [plugin-dir...]
vestra-plugin test  [plugin-dir...]
vestra-plugin build [plugin-dir...] [--version x.y.z]
vestra-plugin pack  [plugin-dir...] [--version x.y.z] [--out dir]
```

- `check`: checks the manifest (every rule above), then a strict type check of the plugin's `.ts` files and `tests/`. It extends the nearest `tsconfig.json` at or above the plugin directory, else built-in strict settings. Hints that do not fail the check (such as an id without an owner prefix) are printed.
- `build`: checks, then writes `dist/`: `.ts` files with types stripped (relative imports rewritten to `.js`), `.slint`, `.mjs` and data files copied, the manifest's `icon`, `readme` and `changelog` (and `README.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` when present) copied, `dist/manifest.json` with the version (from `--version`, else the manifest, else `package.json`). Tests, `node_modules/`, other Markdown and `package*.json` are left out. A runtime import of `@vestra-player/sdk` fails the build.
- `pack`: builds, then packs `dist/` as `<id>-<version>.vxp` (a zip with `manifest.json` at its root; the same input gives the same bytes) and prints its size and sha256. This is the file users install and repositories list.
- Runtime npm dependencies must be bundled: set `"vestra": { "bundle": true }` (or `{ "bundle": { "external": [...] } }`) in the plugin's `package.json` and add `esbuild` as a dev dependency. `"vestra": { "assets": ["vendor"] }` copies extra files verbatim.

During development no build is needed: start the player with `--plugin <plugin-dir>` (repeatable) to run `main.ts` directly.

### Versions

| SDK package | Plugin `apiVersion` | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `1.x`       | `vestra/1`          | Minor releases only add backwards-compatible API; patch releases fix documentation and bugs.                                                                                                                                                |
| `1.1`       | `vestra/1`          | The additions need player 0.2.0: set `"minPlayerVersion": "0.2.0"` when you use them.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `1.3`       | `vestra/1`          | Menu ids (`@video`), `Theme.danger` and removing a video chain with `[]` need player 0.3.0: set `"minPlayerVersion": "0.3.0"` when you use them.                                                                                            |
| `1.4`       | `vestra/1`          | One exception to "only add": `ThemeId` lost the second palette and is `"vestra"` only. A plugin that compared with or set the removed id fails to type check; the player treats that id as `vestra`, so already built plugins keep running. |
| `1.5`       | `vestra/1`          | The light palette `vestra-light` and `@vestra/icons.slint` need player 0.4.0: set `"minPlayerVersion": "0.4.0"` when you use them.                                                                                                          |

A breaking change to the plugin API gets a new `apiVersion` and a new major version of this package. The `@vestra-player/sdk/runtime` entry is for the player only and is not covered by semver.

## Concept: Windows, panels, settings pages, dialogs and the OSD

A plugin can show its own user interface in five places. Three of them are drawn by the plugin's own Slint files: **tool windows**, **panels** and **settings pages**. Two are drawn by the player or the system from plain values: **dialogs** and the **on-screen display (OSD)**. This page explains what each one is, how to choose, how each one lives and dies, how Slint and TypeScript talk to each other, and what to watch out for.

It assumes you have written a first plugin (Getting started). For every method's parameters and errors, follow the links into the API reference.

### The five surfaces

```text
┌─ main window ─────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────┐
│ ① OSD message (top left, 2 s)                         │             │
│ ① OSD info blocks (one per plugin, under the message) │  ② sidebar  │
│                                                       │    panel    │
│            video area                                 │             │
│            ② backdrop panel while there is no video   │             │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤             │
│ ② bottom bar panel                                    │             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────┘

  separate operating-system windows:
  ③ tool windows · ④ the Options window with the settings pages
  ② the sidebar panel when it is detached (floating) · ⑤ dialogs
```

**① On-screen display** (plugin.osd, capability `ui.osd`). Text the player draws over the top-left of the video: a one-line message that disappears after 2 seconds (osd.show), and one multi-line information block per plugin that stays until you clear it (osd.panel). It takes no input and needs no Slint.

**② Panels** (plugin.panels, `ui.mount`). A Slint component the player places _inside its main window_: in the **bottom bar** under the video, in the **sidebar** on the right (which the user can detach into a floating window of its own), or as the **backdrop** drawn over the video area while there is no video picture. A panel is part of the player's layout: it moves, resizes, hides in fullscreen and auto-hides with the player's own controls. Each plugin mounts at most one panel.

**③ Tool windows** (plugin.windows, `ui.window`). A separate, top-level operating-system window owned by the plugin: it has its own title bar, the user can move it, resize it (if the Slint file allows) and close it, and it is not modal: the main window keeps playing and keeps taking input while it is open. A plugin can have any number of them.

**④ Settings pages** (plugin.settings, `ui.settings`). A page in the player's **Options** window, under one of nine fixed categories (General, Playback, Subtitles, Video, Audio, Input, Appearance, Plugins, Other). The player owns the window (its tree, its Close button, its size); the plugin provides the page's content. At most 8 pages per plugin.

**⑤ Dialogs** (plugin.dialogs, `ui.dialog`). The system's own dialogs: a confirmation alert (confirm) and the open-file, open-folder and save-file dialogs. The plugin passes text and gets an answer back; it does not draw anything. Only one dialog is open at a time, player-wide.

### Choosing a surface

| You want to…                                                                                  | Use                                                                        | Why not the others                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Confirm that something happened ("Bookmark added", "Speed 1.5×")                              | OSD message                                                                | A window or dialog would interrupt; the message vanishes by itself.                      |
| Show a few live numbers while playing (bitrate, A/B loop points)                              | OSD info block                                                             | Needs no Slint and no focus; drawn over the video, also in fullscreen.                   |
| Content that belongs to the player and stays visible: a playlist, chapters, a custom seek bar | Panel (sidebar or bottom bar)                                              | It follows the main window's layout and fullscreen; a tool window would float elsewhere. |
| Cover art or an idle screen while nothing is playing                                          | Panel in the `backdrop` slot                                               | It replaces the black video area; one plugin at a time.                                  |
| A tool the user opens, uses and closes: picture adjustments, an inspector, an editor          | Tool window                                                                | It has its own title bar and size and does not take space from the video.                |
| Preferences that rarely change                                                                | Settings page                                                              | Users look for preferences in Options; the player keeps the window and its navigation.   |
| A yes/no question before something destructive                                                | Dialogs.confirm dialogs.confirm               | Native look and keyboard handling (Enter, Escape); no Slint file.                        |
| A file or folder from the user                                                                | Dialogs.openFile dialogs.openFile and friends | The system dialog is the only one users trust with paths.                                |

Two rules of thumb:

- **Prefer the smallest surface that works.** An OSD message before a dialog, a settings page before a tool window. Every window the user has to close is a cost.
- **Panels are shared space.** There is one sidebar, one bottom bar and one backdrop for all plugins. The sidebar holds several panels as tabs (the player draws the tab strip while there are two or more; showing, hiding and detaching apply to all of them). The bottom bar and the backdrop hold one: while one plugin's panel is there, another plugin's mount rejects with `conflict`, which does not fail its activation. Mount a panel only when the plugin's main purpose is to live there.

### Life cycles

Every surface is a **handle** owned by the Scope that created it. Disposing the scope (or the plugin stopping) releases it: windows close, panels are unmounted, settings pages leave the Options window, the info block disappears. A plugin never has to clean up its interface by hand.

#### Tool window

```text
 windows.create(file)       nothing on screen yet; bind callbacks and properties now
        │  view.on(), view.bind(), view.set()
        ▼
 ┌──────────────┐   show()   ┌──────────────┐   hide()   ┌──────────────┐
 │    closed    │──────────▶│   visible    │──────────▶│    hidden     │
 │ opened=false │           │ opened=true  │◀──────────│ opened=true  │
 └──────────────┘           └──────────────┘   show()   └──────────────┘
        ▲                       │       │
        │  close()              │       │  the user: title-bar close button,
        │  (no onClose)         │       │  ⌘W (macOS), Ctrl+W or Ctrl+F4 (Windows)
        └───────────────────────┘       │  → onClose listeners run
        ▲                               │
        └───────────────────────────────┘
 dispose(), the scope disposed, the plugin stopped: closed for good (no onClose)
```

- `create()` only makes a local handle. The first `show()` compiles the Slint file and opens the window with the properties you bound or set so far, so no default values flash.
- Callbacks are registered when the window opens: bind every callback name with on() **before the first `show()`**. Binding a new name while the window is open throws.
- `close()` and a user close both destroy the window instance. The handle stays usable: the next `show()` opens a **fresh** instance with the current properties (whatever the user typed into fields that the plugin did not record is gone).
- Only a user close calls onClose. Stop timers and polling there.

#### Panel

```text
 panels.mount(slot, file)
        │  on() / bind() in the same tick are part of the first values
        ▼  (next microtask)
 ui.mount ──▶ the player queues it and rebuilds its main window with the panel
        │                                                   │
        ▼ ready resolves                                    ▼ ready rejects
 mounted ── user / setVisible(false) / no space ──▶ hidden   (ui-prepare, conflict,
    │    ◀─ user / setVisible(true) / toggle() ───          busy, unavailable…)
    │
    ├─ sidebar only: setDetached(true) / the user ──▶ floating window
    │     closing the floating window = setVisible(false)
    │
 dispose() / plugin stops ──▶ unmounted; the main window is rebuilt without it
```

- **Mounting rebuilds the main window.** The player compiles its main window together with every mounted panel, so mounting or unmounting any panel (from any plugin) rebuilds it. The player restores each panel's bridge properties to the last values its plugin wrote, but anything kept only inside the Slint component (a scroll position, a `property` the plugin never writes, the text of a field the plugin does not mirror) starts over. The same happens when the sidebar is detached or attached: the floating window holds a new instance of the component.
- The position (`plugin.panels.bottom`, `.sidebar`) is separate from the panel: it has the user's preference (`preferred`), whether it is on screen now (`effective`) and why not (`reason`), and its tabs (`panels`). Any plugin with `ui.mount` can read and toggle it, so a "Show playlist" command can live in a different plugin than the playlist. The panel's own state (Panel.state) adds whether its tab is the current one (`reason: "otherTab"` when not); Panel.toggle brings a background tab forward instead of closing the sidebar.
- The player remembers the sidebar's visibility, width, detached state and floating window position across launches.

#### Settings page

```text
 settings.page(file, { id, category, title })
        ▼  (next microtask)
 settings.register ──▶ the player compiles the page on its own ──▶ ready
                                                          (or ui-prepare, invalid…)
 the user opens Options, or settings.show(id)
        ▼
 the Options window is built from every registered page
        │  pages added or removed while it is open: rebuilt, properties restored
        ▼
 dispose() / plugin stops ──▶ page removed (the window shows a neighbouring page)
```

- The Options window belongs to the player. The page exists from `ready` on, whether or not the window is open; property writes while it is closed are kept and applied when it opens.
- The page is compiled alone at registration, so a broken page fails its own `ready` and not the whole window.

#### Dialogs and the OSD

- Dialogs are one call each: the promise resolves when the user answers. There is no time limit and no way to close a dialog from code. Playback continues while it is open; command key bindings pause.
- The OSD message is fire-and-forget; a newer message (from any plugin) replaces the current one. The info block is a handle: `set(text)` shows or changes it, `set(null)` hides it, disposing removes it.

### How Slint and TypeScript talk

The plugin process and the user interface run in different processes: your TypeScript runs in the plugin's Node.js process, the Slint files run inside the player. They exchange exactly two kinds of messages:

| Direction   | Slint side                               | TypeScript side                                                                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| plugin → UI | `in property` or `in-out property`       | View.set set() or View.bind bind() |
| UI → plugin | `callback name(args);` returning nothing | View.on on("name", handler)                                     |

A tool window (Window), a panel (Panel) and a settings page (SettingsPage) all share this View surface. Nothing else crosses: the plugin cannot call Slint functions or read a property back; a value the user changes reaches the plugin only through a callback.

#### Where the properties live: component or global

- **A tool window file exports exactly one component**, usually `export component X inherits Window`. Its properties and callbacks are declared on that component. The window is yours, so the component is the window.
- **A panel or settings page file exports one component and one global.** The player composes your component into a window it owns (the main window, the floating sidebar window, the Options window), so the component instance is not a stable address: a new instance is made whenever the main window is rebuilt or the sidebar moves to or from its floating window. The **global** is the bridge: properties and callbacks are declared on it, the component reads and calls them (`ListBridge.rows`, `ListBridge.select(index)`), and the plugin talks to the global. The SDK finds the two names from the file's `export component` and `export global` lines.

```slint
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";

export global ListBridge {
    in property <[string]> rows;
    in property <int> selected;
    callback select(int);
    callback context-menu(float, float);
}

export component ListPanel inherits Rectangle {
    background: Theme.bg-list;
    min-width: 200px;
    VerticalLayout {
        for row[index] in ListBridge.rows: Rectangle {
            height: 20px;
            background: index == ListBridge.selected ? Theme.selected-bg : transparent;
            Text {
                x: 6px;
                text: (index + 1) + ". " + row;
                color: index == ListBridge.selected ? Theme.text : Theme.text-list;
                font-size: Theme.font-body;
                vertical-alignment: center;
            }
            TouchArea {
                pointer-event(event) => {
                    if event.kind == PointerEventKind.down {
                        ListBridge.select(index);
                    }
                    if event.kind == PointerEventKind.up && event.button == PointerEventButton.right {
                        ListBridge.context-menu((self.absolute-position.x + self.mouse-x) / 1px,
                            (self.absolute-position.y + self.mouse-y) / 1px);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // Takes the space below the rows. Without it the layout's maximum
        // height (three 20px rows) would cap the player's main window.
        Rectangle { vertical-stretch: 1; }
    }
}
```

Helper components without `export` are allowed in every file. The player appends a line that exports its palette to every plugin file, so do not declare anything named `VestraPalette`.

#### Names and values

- Write names in camelCase or kebab-case in TypeScript: the SDK turns every capital letter into `-` plus the lower-case letter (`canMark` → `can-mark`, `strengthChanged` → `strength-changed`). Fields inside struct values are **not** converted, so spell struct fields exactly as the Slint struct does (and without `_`, which Slint treats as `-`).
- Values must be JSON: booleans, numbers, strings, arrays (Slint models) and objects (Slint structs). Two exceptions: an image from ui.image, only as the **whole** value of an `image` property (nested in an array or object it is `invalid`), and a document from ui.markdown wherever the Slint type is `[MarkdownBlock]`: the whole value, or (SDK 1.5.4, the player after 0.4.0) a field at any depth, such as the `body` of each message in a chat list.
- Every name must exist in the Slint file. Writing a property the file does not declare makes a tool window's `show()` or a panel's `ready` fail, and in a settings page it keeps the Options window from opening; for a tool window, so does a callback bound with `on()` that the file does not declare. Once the view is open, such writes are reported to onError.

#### set, bind and the update pass

`set(props)` writes now. `bind(() => props)` declares that properties should _always_ equal a function of your state; the SDK re-evaluates every bound function in an **update pass** and sends only the values that changed.

|                  | `set({ x })`                                                                            | `bind(() => ({ x }))`                                                                 |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| When it is sent  | Immediately (in the next write).                                                        | In every update pass, if `x` differs from the last value sent.                        |
| Same value again | Sent again. Use this to pull a control back to the model value after the user moved it. | Not sent. A field the user edited stays as the user left it until your value changes. |
| Write fails      | Retried with back-off (0.25 s doubling up to 30 s).                                     | Not repeated until the value changes.                                                 |
| Typical use      | One-off values: a document, a reset.                                                    | Everything derived from plugin state: labels, enabled flags, lists, status lines.     |

Update passes run:

- after every handler the SDK calls (a command's `run`, a view callback, an `onChange` listener) returns, and again when its promise settles;
- after player, subtitle, panel position, filter and export state changes;
- when you call plugin.update().

Several requests in the same microtask are merged into one pass, and each view has at most one write in flight: values that change meanwhile are merged into the next write. So binding a value that changes 60 times a second costs at most one write per round trip, never a queue.

The rule to remember: **state you change after an `await` inside a handler appears only when the handler finishes**, unless something else triggers a pass. Call `plugin.update()` right after changing it (see Keep a slider responsive while dragging).

#### Two-way controls

A control whose value both the user and the plugin change (a slider, a switch, a text field, a combo box) needs a **two-way binding to an `in-out` property**:

```slint
in-out property <float> strength;
callback strength-changed(float);
Slider {
    value <=> root.strength;                          // two-way: never `value: root.strength`
    changed(value) => { root.strength-changed(value); }
}
```

A one-way binding (`value: root.strength`) is broken by Slint the first time the user moves the control; after that the plugin's writes no longer move it. In a panel or settings page the same applies to the global: `checked <=> MyBridge.enabled`.

### Theme and widgets

Plugin Slint files import the player's design tokens and widgets:

```slint
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";
import { Icon } from "@vestra/icons.slint";
import { Button, Slider, ToolTipArea, UrlInputRow } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";
import { MarkdownView, MarkdownBlocks, MarkdownBlock } from "@vestra/markdown.slint";
```

- **Colours follow the player's palette.** The player has two palettes, `vestra` (dark, the default) and `vestra-light` (player 0.4.0, SDK 1.5), both drawn from the logo's colours: a magenta accent, cyan for what is playing, an amber → magenta → violet → cyan gradient for fills (see plugin.appearance). It sets the palette on every view before it appears and again when the user switches, so `Theme` colours change with it. Colours you hard-code do not. `Theme` properties are read-only.
- **The video area is dark in every palette** (`Theme.bg-video`). Text or icons you draw over the video (a backdrop, an overlay) use light colours, not `Theme.text`, which is dark in `vestra-light`.
- Colour tokens: `bg-bar`, `bg-video`, `bg-list`, `bg-panel`, `line`, `hover-bg`, `press-bg`, `selected-bg`, `text`, `text-dim`, `text-list`, `text-played`, `accent`, `accent-press`, `accent-disabled`, `icon-disabled`, `playing`, `button-bg`, `button-hover`, `button-press`, `button-disabled`, `accent-fill` (a gradient brush) and `danger` (errors and destructive actions: a failed status line, a Delete button; player 0.3.0, SDK 1.3).
- Fonts: every window uses the system UI font (Slint falls back per character for scripts it lacks, CJK included); `Theme.font-mono` is the system's monospace family (Menlo on macOS, Consolas on Windows). Sizes: `font-xs` 9px, `font-body` 11px, `font-tab` 12px, `font-title` 13px.
- Control sizes and spacing: `button-height` 21px, `input-height` 21px, `form-row-gap` 26px, `dialog-padding` 14px, `radius-control` 4px (controls, rows, hover plates), `radius-panel` 8px (menus, panels) and others; the full list is the SDK's read-only copy in [`slint/vestra/theme.slint`](https://github.com/vestrasys/vestra-player-sdk/blob/main/slint/vestra/theme.slint). Player 0.4.0 rounded the corners (3px and 6px before).
- **Icons** (player 0.4.0, SDK 1.5): `Icon { name: "play"; color: Theme.text; }` draws one icon of the player's own set: round-capped 1.5px lines (1.25px for small glyphs), never filled, in the icon's own box (its default size; set `width` and `height` to scale). Names: `play`, `pause`, `stop`, `back`, `forward`, `open`, `volume`, `mute`, `playlist`, `detach`, `attach`, `close`, `failed`, `move-top`, `move-up`, `move-down`, `move-bottom`, `search`, `chapter`, `bookmark`, `check-task`, `check-box`, `menu-check`, `submenu`, `scroll-up`, `scroll-down`, `caret-down`, `sort-asc`, `sort-desc`, `tag-remove`, `preview-play`, `add`, `remove`, `sort`; `Icons.commands(name)`, `Icons.box-width(name)`, `Icons.box-height(name)` and `Icons.line(name)` give the path data for your own `Path`. Plugins that use it set `"minPlayerVersion": "0.4.0"`.
- Every plugin file is compiled with Slint's `fluent-dark` style, so `std-widgets.slint` controls (`CheckBox`, `ComboBox`, `Switch`, `LineEdit`…) are dark too; in `vestra-light` the player switches them to their light colours (`Palette.color-scheme`) at run time. Do not set `Palette.color-scheme` yourself.
- **Markdown** (`@vestra/markdown.slint`): `MarkdownView` scrolls one document; `MarkdownBlocks` (SDK 1.5.4, the player after 0.4.0) draws one without scrolling, as tall as its content, for your own layout or a `ListView` row. Both take `blocks: [MarkdownBlock]`, report `link-clicked(url)`, and with `code-copy: true` (default `false`) put a 复制 button on code blocks that reports `copy-code(code)`; copy it with plugin.clipboard. A chat window:

  ```slint
  import { ListView } from "std-widgets.slint";
  import { MarkdownBlocks, MarkdownBlock } from "@vestra/markdown.slint";
  export struct Message { id: string, role: string, body: [MarkdownBlock] }
  export component Chat inherits Window {
      in property <[Message]> messages;
      callback copy-code(string);
      ListView {
          for message in root.messages: VerticalLayout {
              padding: 8px;
              MarkdownBlocks {
                  blocks: message.body;
                  code-copy: true;
                  copy-code(code) => { root.copy-code(code); }
              }
          }
      }
  }
  ```

  Write the list with a document per row (`messages: [{ id, role, body: await plugin.ui.markdown(text) }]`). The player parses only the documents that changed and updates the list in place (rows added or removed at the end, a growing message's changed blocks), so re-sending the whole list on every streamed chunk keeps the scroll position and costs little.
- For editor support, point the Slint language server's `libraryPaths` at the copy in the SDK package: `{ "vestra": "node_modules/@vestra-player/sdk/slint/vestra" }`.

### Sizes

All sizes are logical pixels (Slint's `px`): one logical pixel is two physical pixels on a Retina display or at 200 % scaling.

| Surface          | Width                                                                                                                   | Height                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tool window      | The `Window` component's `width` (fixed, not resizable), or `preferred-width` (initial) within `min-width`/`max-width`. | Same with `height`. The title is the component's `title`.                                                                                                      |
| Bottom bar       | The video column's width.                                                                                               | The component's preferred height (within its minimum and maximum). It may draw above its slot into the video area (negative `y`); the player does not clip it. |
| Sidebar          | Set by the user with the splitter (at least 317; the video keeps at least 318).                                         | The window's full height.                                                                                                                                      |
| Floating sidebar | 300 by default, at least 300.                                                                                           | 408 by default, at least 250.                                                                                                                                  |
| Backdrop         | The whole video area.                                                                                                   | The whole video area.                                                                                                                                          |
| Settings page    | 440.                                                                                                                    | The component's height; the Options window scrolls taller pages.                                                                                               |

The operating system places a tool window when it opens; the player does not remember tool window positions or sizes, and the API cannot read or set them. To keep a tool window's _content_ across runs, see Remember a window's state between runs.

### Focus and keyboard

- **Command key bindings belong to the main window.** A binding from CommandOptions.bindings fires while the main window or the floating sidebar window has focus (and the key was not taken by a focused control, such as Space in a text field). It does **not** fire while a tool window or the Options window has focus. Keys inside your own window are Slint's job: use a `FocusScope` with `key-pressed`, or a button's default action.
- A binding with `focus: "panel"` fires only while this plugin's panel (docked or floating) has focus, and wins over global bindings there.
- **Standard close keys are not bindings.** ⌘W on macOS, Ctrl+W and Ctrl+F4 on Windows close a tool window, the floating sidebar or the Options window exactly like the title-bar button (a tool window's `onClose` runs). The player takes these keys before Slint sees them, even when a text field has focus, so neither your Slint handlers nor your bindings receive them. The main window does not react to them, so a `Ctrl+W` binding still fires there.
- While a menu or a system dialog is open, bindings pause.

### Platform differences

|                                                | macOS                                                                                 | Windows                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Close a tool window, floating sidebar, Options | ⌘W                                                                                    | Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `dialogs.confirm`                              | An `NSAlert` sheet on the active player window (the tool window that asked, usually). | A task dialog owned by the active player window, titled "Vestra Player"; `destructive` shows a warning icon; a `checkbox` is asked as a second yes/no dialog after the user confirms. |
| `Theme.font-mono`                              | Menlo                                                                                 | Consolas                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `DropModifiers.cmd`                            | ⌘                                                                                     | Ctrl                                                                                                                                                                                  |

The API is the same on both systems. Other systems answer `dialogs.confirm` with `unsupported`. When the player runs without a user interface (headless, as in some automated setups), opening windows, mounting panels, dialogs, the OSD and `settings.show` fail with `unavailable`.

### Common pitfalls

- **A window callback bound after the first `show()`.** It throws. Bind all callbacks right after `create()`; re-binding a name that already has a handler is fine.
- **A one-way binding on a control.** `value: root.x` stops following the plugin after the user touches the control. Use `in-out` and `<=>`.
- **`set()` inside a frequent loop.** `set` always sends, even an unchanged value; a periodic `set` of a slider value pulls the thumb back from under the user's pointer. Use `bind` for anything derived from state.
- **Changes after an `await` do not appear.** The update pass runs when the handler finishes; call `plugin.update()` for progress in between.
- **State only inside a panel component.** It is lost when the main window is rebuilt or the sidebar detaches. Keep anything that matters in bridge properties written by the plugin.
- **User edits the plugin does not record.** A settings page or tool window is rebuilt from the plugin's last written values; an `in-out` property the user changed without a callback updating your model reverts. Handle the callback and keep the value in your state (and `bind` it).
- **Hard-coded colours.** They do not follow the palette. Use `Theme.*`, and `Theme.danger` for errors.
- **A `Ctrl+W` default binding.** It never fires in tool windows and floating panels. Pick another key.
- **Two of a kind.** One panel per plugin, one backdrop per player, one OSD info block per plugin, one open dialog at a time (`busy`).
- **Slot state without `events`.** PanelSlot.state, appearance.theme and their `onChange` listeners follow other plugins and the user only with the `events` capability.

### Testing

`TestHost` from `@vestra-player/sdk/testing` runs a plugin without the player and records its interface: `host.window(id)` (`props`, `callbacks`, `visible`, `emit(callback, ...args)`, `userClose()`), `host.mounted()` for the panel, `host.settingsPage(id)` and `host.settings`, `host.osd` (messages shown), `host.confirms` and `host.dialogAnswers`. Property names in `props` are the Slint (kebab-case) names. The test host does not compile Slint files; check them by running the plugin in the player.

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";

async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let count = 0;
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/counter.slint");
  window.bind(() => ({ label: `Clicked ${count} times` }));
  window.on("clicked", () => count++);
  await window.show();
}

test("the label counts clicks", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    capabilities: ["ui.window"],
  });
  host.window("counter").emit("clicked");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(host.window("counter").props["label"], "Clicked 1 times");
  await stop();
});
```

## How-to: Keep a slider responsive while dragging

**Goal:** a slider in your window drives something live (a video filter, the volume, a preview), the effect follows the pointer while the user drags, and nothing lags behind or queues up.

A slider reports every pointer movement, often more than 60 times a second. Each report is a callback in your plugin. The plugin stays responsive if every callback only **records the newest value and hands it to something that keeps only the newest value**. It stutters when every callback starts its own slow request and the requests queue up behind each other.

### The complete example

A **Brightness** window with a slider from −1 to 1, a value label and a Reset button. The video follows the slider while it moves; an on-screen message reports the value when the user lets go.

`manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "examples.brightness",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.3.0",
  "capabilities": [
    "commands",
    "ui.window",
    "ui.osd",
    "processing.video",
    "playback.read",
    "events"
  ]
}
```

`ui/brightness.slint`:

```slint
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";
import { Button, Slider } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";

export component BrightnessWindow inherits Window {
    title: "Brightness";
    width: 300px;
    background: Theme.bg-panel;

    // Written by the plugin and by the slider: in-out, bound two-way below.
    in-out property <float> brightness;
    in property <string> label;
    callback brightness-changed(float); // every pointer move
    callback brightness-released(float); // once, when the button is released
    callback reset();

    HorizontalLayout {
        padding: Theme.dialog-padding;
        spacing: 8px;
        Slider {
            minimum: -1;
            maximum: 1;
            value <=> root.brightness;
            changed(value) => { root.brightness-changed(value); }
            released(value) => { root.brightness-released(value); }
        }
        Text {
            width: 36px;
            text: root.label;
            color: Theme.text;
            font-size: Theme.font-body;
            horizontal-alignment: right;
            vertical-alignment: center;
        }
        Button {
            text: "Reset";
            small: true;
            clicked => { root.reset(); }
        }
    }
}
```

`main.ts`:

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let brightness = 0; // the model: −1–1, 0 = unchanged

  // A filter keeps one request in flight and sends only the newest value.
  const filter = plugin.video.filter("brightness");
  const apply = () =>
    filter.set([
      { kind: "eq", brightness, contrast: 1, saturation: 1, gamma: 1 },
    ]);

  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/brightness.slint");
  // Derived from the model: sent only when it changes.
  window.bind(() => ({ brightness, label: brightness.toFixed(2) }));

  window.on("brightnessChanged", (value: number) => {
    brightness = Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, value)); // record the newest value…
    apply(); // …and hand it on; no await
  });
  window.on("brightnessReleased", () => {
    void plugin.osd.show(`Brightness ${brightness.toFixed(2)}`); // once per drag
  });
  window.on("reset", () => {
    brightness = 0; // the bound value moves the slider back
    apply();
  });

  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "brightness",
    path: ["@video", "Brightness…"],
    run: () => window.show(),
  });
}
```

### Why this stays smooth

1. **The callback does not wait.** `brightnessChanged` updates a variable and calls `filter.set()`, which returns at once. The SDK runs the next callback as soon as it arrives.
2. **The expensive part keeps only the newest value.** `filter.set()` has _latest-value_ semantics: while one request is in flight, newer values replace each other and only the last one is sent. A fast drag costs a request per round trip to the player, not one per pointer move, and the video ends exactly where the slider stopped.
3. **The slider's value is bound, not set.** `bind` sends `brightness` only when it differs from what was sent last, and the player skips a write that equals what the slider already shows. So the plugin never fights the user's pointer, yet Reset (which changes the model) moves the thumb.
4. **Work that should happen once happens on release.** The on-screen message (and anything like saving or logging) waits for `brightnessReleased`, which fires once per drag.

The Slint side needs two things: an `in-out` property and a two-way binding (`value <=> root.brightness`). With a one-way binding (`value: root.brightness`) Slint breaks the binding the first time the user drags, and Reset stops moving the thumb.

### Which calls keep only the newest value

| Latest value wins (safe on every move)                                                                                 | One request per call (do not call on every move)                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| VideoFilter VideoFilter`.set`, AudioFilter AudioFilter`.set` | Player.seek player.seek: use Player.scrub player.scrub() and `Scrub.seek` for a seek slider |
| Player.setOutput player.setOutput (volume, mute)                                          | `player.setRate` and other player controls                                                                                                            |
| `Scrub.seek` (about one seek per display frame)                                                                        | Osd.show osd.show: show a message on release                                                                             |
| View properties (`bind`, `set`), OsdPanel.set OsdPanel.set                                | `JsonStore.save` is debounced (300 ms), so it is fine; anything you write yourself is not                                                             |

### When the slow part is your own code

If a move triggers your own asynchronous work (rendering a preview with `plugin.tools.run`, a network request), do not `await` it per callback: the SDK starts every callback without waiting for the previous one, so slow runs overlap and can finish out of order, leaving an _older_ result on screen. Give that work latest-value semantics yourself:

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** Run `work` for the newest value only: one run at a time; values that arrive meanwhile replace each other. */
export function latest<T>(work: (value: T) => Promise<void>) {
  let running = false;
  let next: { value: T } | undefined;
  return async (value: T) => {
    next = { value };
    if (running) return; // the running loop picks it up
    running = true;
    try {
      while (next) {
        const current = next.value;
        next = undefined;
        await work(current);
      }
    } finally {
      running = false;
    }
  };
}

declare function renderPreview(strength: number): Promise<string>; // your own slow work

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let preview = "";
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/preview.slint");
  window.bind(() => ({ preview }));
  const refresh = latest(async (strength: number) => {
    preview = await renderPreview(strength);
    plugin.update(); // changed after an await: send it now
  });
  window.on("strengthChanged", (strength: number) => refresh(strength));
}
```

`plugin.update()` matters here. The SDK re-evaluates bound properties after a callback returns and again when its promise settles; a value you change **after an `await`** inside a longer task is otherwise shown only when that task ends. Call `plugin.update()` whenever such a task has something new to show.

## How-to: Remember a window's state between runs

**Goal:** a tool window comes back the way the user left it: its controls hold the last values, and if it was open when the player quit, it opens again at the next start.

A tool window keeps nothing by itself: closing it destroys the window instance, and the plugin process ends with the player. Keep the state in your plugin, store it with plugin.storage.json, show it with `bind`, and reopen the window during activation.

### The complete example

The **Brightness** window from Keep a slider responsive while dragging, now remembering the brightness and whether the window was open. The manifest is the same as there, without `ui.osd`:

```json
{
  "id": "examples.brightness",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.3.0",
  "capabilities": [
    "commands",
    "ui.window",
    "processing.video",
    "playback.read",
    "events"
  ]
}
```

`ui/brightness.slint` is unchanged: it declares `in-out property <float> brightness`, `in property <string> label` and the callbacks `brightness-changed(float)`, `brightness-released(float)` and `reset()` (the full file is on the slider page).

`main.ts`:

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** Everything the plugin remembers, in <dataDirectory>/brightness.json. */
interface Saved {
  /** −1–1, 0 = unchanged. */
  brightness: number;
  /** The window was open when the player quit. */
  open: boolean;
}

const DEFAULTS: Saved = { brightness: 0, open: false };

/** A missing, broken or outdated file falls back to DEFAULTS. */
function isSaved(value: unknown): value is Saved {
  const v = value as Partial<Saved> | null;
  return (
    typeof v === "object" &&
    v !== null &&
    typeof v.brightness === "number" &&
    Math.abs(v.brightness) <= 1 &&
    typeof v.open === "boolean"
  );
}

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  // 1. Load: read once, synchronously; defaults if there is no valid file.
  const store = plugin.storage.json<Saved>("brightness", {
    defaults: DEFAULTS,
    validate: isSaved,
  });
  /** Change part of the state; the file is written 300 ms after the last change. */
  const remember = (patch: Partial<Saved>) =>
    store.save({ ...store.value, ...patch });

  const filter = plugin.video.filter("brightness");
  const apply = () =>
    filter.set([
      {
        kind: "eq",
        brightness: store.value.brightness,
        contrast: 1,
        saturation: 1,
        gamma: 1,
      },
    ]);
  apply(); // the effect is back before the window is

  // 2. Show: the window always displays the stored state.
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/brightness.slint");
  window.bind(() => ({
    brightness: store.value.brightness,
    label: store.value.brightness.toFixed(2),
  }));
  window.on("brightnessChanged", (value: number) => {
    remember({ brightness: Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, value)) });
    apply();
  });
  window.on("reset", () => {
    remember({ brightness: 0 });
    apply();
  });

  // 3. Track whether it is open: only the user closing it counts as "closed".
  window.onClose(() => remember({ open: false }));
  const open = async () => {
    await window.show();
    remember({ open: true });
  };
  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "brightness",
    path: ["@video", "Brightness…"],
    run: open,
  });

  // 4. Restore: reopen it if it was open when the player quit.
  if (store.value.open) await open().catch(() => remember({ open: false }));
}
```

### How it works

- **Load once, at activation.** `storage.json` reads `<dataDirectory>/brightness.json` synchronously when it is created. A file that cannot be parsed or fails `validate` is renamed to `brightness.json.bad-<timestamp>` and `defaults` is used, so a damaged or older file never breaks the plugin. Always pass a `validate` function: the file is outside your control.
- **Bind the stored value, not a copy.** `window.bind` reads `store.value` in every update pass, so whatever changes the state (a callback, Reset, a command) updates the window, and a window opened later starts with the current values.
- **Save on every change; the store debounces.** `save()` replaces `store.value` at once and writes the file 300 ms after the last call (a temporary file, then a rename). Dragging the slider writes the file once, after the drag. When the plugin stops (the player quits, the user disables the plugin), the store is flushed, so the last value is not lost.
- **"Open" means "the user did not close it".** `onClose` runs only when the user closes the window (title-bar button, ⌘W, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4). When the player quits, the plugin stops and its windows close _without_ `onClose`, so `open` stays `true` and the window comes back next time. That is the behaviour users expect from an application's tool windows.
- **Restore after binding.** The window is created and bound before `open()` runs, so it opens with the stored values and without flashing defaults. If it cannot open (for example in a player without a user interface), the plugin forgets that it was open instead of failing activation.

### What you cannot restore

- **Position and size.** The operating system places a tool window when it opens. The player does not remember tool window frames, and the API has no way to read or set them; the window's size comes from its Slint file (`width`, `preferred-width` and so on).
- **State that only Slint knows.** Text in a field, a scroll position or a selected tab survives only if a callback reports it to the plugin and the plugin stores it and writes it back as a property, as `brightness` does here.

### Variations

- **Several windows from one file** (one per document, created with `windows.create(file, { id })`): store an object keyed by the window id and restore each one.
- **Preferences rather than state:** a choice such as "reopen my windows at startup" belongs on a settings page (plugin.settings.page) that reads and writes the same store (the `SettingsPage` reference has an example).
- **Large or binary data:** write your own files in plugin.dataDirectory (to a temporary name, then rename) and keep only small settings in `storage.json`.

## API: @vestra-player/sdk

The Vestra Player plugin API (`apiVersion: "vestra/1"`), types only.

A plugin's entry module default-exports `activate`. The player creates
the Plugin object and passes it in; a plugin never imports SDK
code at run time (a built plugin contains only its own code, and
`vestra-plugin build` fails on a runtime import of this package), so
import with `import type`.

Start with Plugin and Scope: every module
(`plugin.commands`, `plugin.player`, `plugin.windows`…) hangs off them and
documents the manifest capability it needs. Errors are described at
PluginError. Tests use `@vestra-player/sdk/testing`.

### Disposable

Anything that owns player-side or local resources: every handle the API
returns (commands, windows, panels, filters, snapshots, listeners…).

A handle belongs to the Scope that created it and is disposed with
that scope, so most plugins never call `dispose()` themselves. Call it to
release one resource early. Disposing twice is harmless, and `dispose()`
never rejects: failures are only written to the plugin log.

What disposal does depends on the handle: a Command leaves the menu
and the binding table, a Window closes, a Panel is
unmounted, a VideoFilter / AudioFilter withdraws this
plugin's chain, a Snapshot is released, an unfinished
ExportJob is cancelled, a Stream stops, a Resolver
is unregistered (aborting resolutions in flight), a JsonStore
flushes, a running `tools.run` process is killed and a listener is
unsubscribed. A Media is the exception: disposing its scope does
**not** close the media; call Media.close for that.

```ts
interface Disposable {
  /** Release the resource. Resolves once the player confirmed the release (or immediately for purely local resources). Never rejects. */
  dispose(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### PluginError

Every API failure is an ordinary `Error` with a stable string `code`.
Branch on `code`, never on `message` (the message is for logs and may
change).

| code | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `stale` | A condition no longer held (the source or the subtitle selection changed); nothing was done. See Conditional. |
| `staleDigest` | PackageCandidate.install: the package's files changed after it was validated; validate it again. |
| `capability` | The manifest does not declare the capability the call needs. |
| `invalid` | A bad argument (out of range, malformed, unknown id). |
| `missing` | The target does not exist (an empty panel position, a missing file, an unknown command). |
| `busy` | The player is still doing a previous call of the same kind (a dialog is open, a step is in flight). |
| `conflict` | Another plugin owns the resource (the sequence provider, the display layer, the backdrop, a menu path), or this plugin already uses the id (a window or command id). |
| `unavailable` | Not possible right now (no ready media, no user interface, fullscreen, a disabled core action). |
| `unsupported` | Not possible on this system, build or source (a platform gap, software rendering, a source that cannot seek, a filter on a generated stream). |
| `backend` | Loading or resolving failed; `message` is the backend's reason. |
| `failed` | The operation ran and failed (`media.ready()` load error, a non-zero `tools.run` exit, the system refused). |
| `replaced` | Accepted, but another source replaced it before it finished. |
| `ended` | Media.ready: the media already played to the end. |
| `noSource` | MediaCapture.capture: nothing is playing to capture. |
| `released`, `disposed` | A Snapshot used after `release()`; an ExportJob handle disposed while something still waited for it. |
| `aborted` | An `AbortSignal` fired (`error.name === "AbortError"`). |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out (`openStream` start-up, `tools.run`, `system.*` after 10 s). |
| `stream`, `device` | `openStream`: the producer failed / the audio device is not ready. |
| `backend-uncertain` | The player's backend blocked a filter stage; call `retry()`. |
| `limit` | A player-wide limit was reached (for example the number of commands), a property value is over the limits of PropValue, or a request is longer than the player's 1 MiB message. |
| `reserved` | Packages.validate, PackageCandidate.install: the id is `vestra` or starts with `vestra.` (any case), which only the player's built-in plugins use (player 0.4.1). |
| `versionMismatch` | The package needs a newer player (`minPlayerVersion`) or another `apiVersion`. |
| `ui-prepare` | The player could not prepare a mounted panel or a settings page (its Slint file does not compile, a bound property is not declared, or another plugin's panel holds the slot); `message` has the diagnostics. |
| `ui` | The player could not apply a property to a tool window or a settings page, or could not build the Options window (a property the Slint file does not declare, a value of the wrong type); `message` has Slint's reason. Also reported to Scope.onError without a request: a callback whose arguments the player could not convert, a property it could not show again when it rebuilt a view (an image file removed since). |
| `host` | Any other failure inside the player; `message` is the player's reason. |
| `disabled` | The plugin is being stopped; pending requests fail with it. |
| `unknown`, `rejected`, `expired` | After a transport problem the SDK could not confirm the outcome (does not happen in normal operation). |

Errors thrown by handlers the SDK invokes go to Scope.onError. A
rejected promise you forgot to `await` is only logged; it never crashes
the plugin process. Requests have no client-side timeout: the player
answers every request or stops the plugin.

```ts
type PluginError = Error & {
  /** The stable failure code (see the table above). */
  code: string;
};
```

### Scope

A group of handles released together.

Plugin is the root scope. Create a child with Scope.scope
for a feature that can be torn down on its own (a dynamic submenu, a
temporary window and its listeners). Both have exactly the same modules;
a handle created through a child belongs only to that child, and
`child.dispose()` releases its handles and deeper children in reverse
creation order.

Capabilities: each module documents the manifest capability it needs.
Reading Scope.window, Scope.app, Scope.appearance
`.theme`, Scope.ui, Scope.tools, Scope.storage and
Scope.system needs none.

```ts
interface Scope extends Disposable {
  /** Menu commands and their default bindings (`commands`). */
  readonly commands: Commands;
  /** Tool windows from `.slint` files (`ui.window`). */
  readonly windows: Windows;
  /** Docked panels: bottom bar, sidebar and backdrop (`ui.mount`). */
  readonly panels: Panels;
  /** Native file dialogs and confirmation alerts (`ui.dialog`). */
  readonly dialogs: Dialogs;
  /** Playback state and controls (`playback.read`, `events`, `playback.control`). */
  readonly player: Player;
  /**
   * Video processing: this plugin's filter chain, the display layer and the GPU render options. All three need `processing.video` and `playback.read`; the filter chain also needs `events` (without it the SDK never sees the media become ready and the chain stays `waiting`).
   */
  readonly video: {
    /**
     * This plugin's video filter chain named `id` (unique within the plugin). Nothing is sent until the first `set()`.
     * @param id - Local name of the chain.
     * @returns A VideoFilter owned by this scope.
     */
    filter(id: string): VideoFilter;
    /**
     * The display layer (needs `processing.video`). The first plugin to call it owns the layer; another plugin's view fails with `conflict` until the owner disposes or stops. A second call in the same plugin throws.
     */
    view(): VideoView;
    /** The GPU renderer's options (needs `processing.video`), owned like the display layer. `failed` with `unsupported` under software rendering. */
    render(): RenderOptions;
  };
  /** Audio processing: this plugin's filter chain and delay (`processing.audio`, `playback.read` and `events`, as for VideoFilter). */
  readonly audio: {
    /**
     * This plugin's audio filter chain named `id` (unique within the plugin). Nothing is sent until the first `set()`.
     * @param id - Local name of the chain.
     * @returns An AudioFilter owned by this scope.
     */
    filter(id: string): AudioFilter;
  };
  /** Subtitle tracks, uploads and style (`subtitles.read`, `subtitles.control`). */
  readonly subtitles: Subtitles;
  /** Frozen snapshots and offline exports (`media.read`, `media.control`). */
  readonly media: MediaCapture;
  /** Page-URL to stream-URL resolvers (`source.resolve`). */
  readonly resolvers: Resolvers;
  /** The installed plugins; validation, installs (`plugins.manage` for changes). */
  readonly packages: Packages;
  /** On-screen messages over the video (`ui.osd`). */
  readonly osd: Osd;
  /** The player's own core playback actions (`commands`). */
  readonly host: Host;
  /** The system clipboard (`clipboard`). */
  readonly clipboard: Clipboard;
  /** Keeping the computer awake while playing (`playback.control`). */
  readonly power: Power;
  /** ffmpeg / ffprobe, run by this plugin's process. */
  readonly tools: Tools;
  /** JSON settings files in `dataDirectory`. */
  readonly storage: Storage;
  /** Show files in the file manager, open files and links. */
  readonly system: System;
  /** Small secrets in the system's secret store (`secrets`). */
  readonly secrets: Secrets;
  /** The main window: fullscreen, video area, size, level, pointer hiding. */
  readonly window: MainWindow;
  /** The player's version and components, and the system it runs on. */
  readonly app: App;
  /** Every command's bindings and the user's overrides (`bindings.manage`). */
  readonly bindings: Bindings;
  /** Runtime images for Slint `image` properties. */
  readonly ui: Ui;
  /** Marks on the seek bar, merged from every plugin's layer. */
  readonly timeline: Timeline;
  /** Files dropped on the video area, by extension (`ui.drop`). */
  readonly drops: Drops;
  /** The player's palette and the saved interface language. */
  readonly appearance: Appearance;
  /** The interface language of this run (read-only). */
  readonly i18n: I18n;
  /** Pages in the player's options window (`ui.settings`). */
  readonly settings: Settings;
  /** A child scope; disposing it releases only what was created through it. The child is itself owned by this scope. */
  scope(): Scope;
  /**
   * Adopt an existing handle: it is disposed together with this scope.
   * @param item - Any Disposable, for example a handle created through another scope.
   * @returns `item` itself, for chaining.
   */
  add<T extends Disposable>(item: T): T;
  /**
   * Run `cleanup` when this scope is disposed (for example `clearInterval` or closing a socket). It may be async; errors are logged.
   * @returns A handle that cancels the registration early (without running `cleanup`).
   */
```
