Values out of range fail with `invalid` (see VideoNode). The
same chain applies to processed snapshots and exports.

```ts
type VideoFilter = Filter<VideoNode[]>;
```

### AudioFilter

This plugin's own audio chain plus its audio delay in 10 ms steps.
From `plugin.audio.filter(id)`; needs `processing.audio`,
`playback.read` and `events`. Same members and rules as
VideoFilter.

`delayMs` is −10000–10000 in multiples of 10; the positive and the
negative delays of all plugins each add up to at most 10000.

```ts
type AudioFilter = Filter<{
  /** The audio chain; `[]` for none. */
  nodes: AudioNode[];
  /** Audio delay in ms, −10000–10000 in steps of 10 (default 0). */
  delayMs?: number;
}>;
```

### ViewSettings

How the video sits in the video area; not part of snapshots or exports.
Defaults: `{ aspect: null, fit: "keep", zoom: 1, panX: 0, panY: 0 }`.

```ts
interface ViewSettings {
  /** Display aspect override 0.25–4; `null` = as the source. */
  aspect: number | null;
  /** keep: letterbox; stretch: fill, distorted; fill: fill, cropped. */
  fit: "keep" | "stretch" | "fill";
  /** 0.25–4 (1 = fit the area). */
  zoom: number;
  /** −1–1, in units of the shown video's width / height. */
  panX: number;
  /** −1–1, in units of the shown video's height. */
  panY: number;
}
```

### VideoView

The display layer, from `plugin.video.view()` (`processing.video`).

Single owner: the first plugin to call `view()` owns it; another plugin's
handle reports `failed` (`conflict`) and retries on each `set`. Values
persist across sources (reset them yourself on a new `sourceId` if
needed); disposing or stopping the owner restores the defaults.
Out-of-range values or unknown fields fail with `invalid` without
sending anything.

```ts
interface VideoView extends Disposable {
  /** Merged into the current settings; last write wins. */
  set(value: Partial<ViewSettings>): void;
  /** Current status (the same four states as filters). */
  readonly status: FilterStatus;
  /** The status changed. */
  onStatus(listener: (status: FilterStatus) => void): Disposable;
}
```

### RenderSettings

GPU renderer options; not part of snapshots or exports.
Defaults: `{ toneMapping: "auto", targetPeak: 203, peakDetect: true, shaders: [], interpolation: false }`.

```ts
interface RenderSettings {
  /** HDR → SDR: "auto" maps HDR sources only; "off" clips without a curve. */
  toneMapping: "auto" | "off" | "bt.2390" | "hable" | "mobius" | "reinhard" | "clip";
  /** SDR display brightness in nits, 100–400. */
  targetPeak: number;
  /** Per-scene peak estimation (where the GPU supports it). */
  peakDetect: boolean;
  /** mpv user shaders (`.glsl`): absolute paths of existing files, at most 16, in order. */
  shaders: string[];
  /** Motion interpolation, resampled to the display's refresh rate. */
  interpolation: boolean;
}
```

### RenderOptions

The GPU renderer's options, from `plugin.video.render()`
(`processing.video`). Single owner, like VideoView; the two are
independent handles.

Platforms: only macOS renders on the GPU. Under software rendering
(Windows, Linux, headless, fallback) every `set` fails with
`unsupported`. macOS OpenGL 4.1 has no compute shaders, so `peakDetect`
is accepted but has no effect; output is always SDR.

```ts
interface RenderOptions extends Disposable {
  /** Merged into the current settings; last write wins. */
  set(value: Partial<RenderSettings>): void;
  /** `failed` with `unsupported` while the player renders in software; `failed` with `failed` when mpv cannot compile a shader (pushed later). */
  readonly status: FilterStatus;
  /** The status changed (including later pushes such as shader compile errors). */
  onStatus(listener: (status: FilterStatus) => void): Disposable;
}
```

### SubtitleTrack

A subtitle track of the current source.

```ts
interface SubtitleTrack {
  /** Stable while the track exists; compare tracks by id. */
  id: string;
  /** Inside the container, or loaded from a file. */
  kind: "embedded" | "external";
  /** The container's subtitle track number, for embedded tracks only. */
  embeddedId?: number;
  /** Track title. */
  title: string;
  /** Language tag, `null` when unknown. */
  language: string | null;
  /** Subtitles.setStyle applies to this track. */
  styleSupported: boolean;
  /** Why the style does not apply, `null` when it does. */
  styleReason: string | null;
  /** Loaded by this plugin, so `remove()` may delete it. */
  owned: boolean;
  /** The backend's codec name, e.g. "subrip", "ass", "hdmv_pgs_subtitle". */
  codec: string | null;
  /** Text cues (subrip, ass, ssa, webvtt, mov_text, text), not bitmaps. */
  text: boolean;
  /** The container stream number (`ffmpeg -map 0:<n>`) of an embedded track, when the player can vouch for it; `null` for external tracks and network sources. */
  streamIndex: number | null;
}
```

### SubtitlesState

The subtitle state of the current source.

```ts
interface SubtitlesState {
  /** The source it belongs to (PlayerState.sourceId). */
  readonly sourceId: number;
  /** The source phase. */
  readonly phase: string;
  /** Every track. */
  readonly tracks: SubtitleTrack[];
  /** The primary subtitle, `null` when off. */
  readonly selected: SubtitleTrack | null;
  /** The secondary subtitle, shown together with `selected`. */
  readonly secondary: SubtitleTrack | null;
  /** Fonts a style can use (`fontId`). */
  readonly fonts: {
    /** Pass as SubtitleStyle.fontId. */
    id: string;
    /** Font family name for display. */
    family: string;
  }[];
  /** The effective style, from whichever plugin set it last. */
  readonly style: SubtitleStyle | null;
  /** Whether the renderer confirmed the selection. */
  readonly trackConfirmation: "waiting" | "applied" | "uncertain";
  /** Whether the renderer confirmed the style. */
  readonly styleConfirmation: "waiting" | "applied" | "uncertain";
  /** The last error, `null` without one. */
  readonly error: string | null;
}
```

### SubtitleConditional

Subtitle calls act on the selection you see; pass `ifCurrent` to pin an older one.

```ts
interface SubtitleConditional {
  /** The subtitle state the call is conditional on; `stale` otherwise. */
  ifCurrent?: SubtitlesState;
}
```

### Subtitles

`plugin.subtitles`: tracks, uploads and style. Reading needs
`subtitles.read`, changes need `subtitles.control`.

```ts
interface Subtitles {
  /** `null` until first read. */
  readonly state: SubtitlesState | null;
  /** The subtitle state changed. */
  onChange(listener: (state: SubtitlesState) => void): Disposable;
  /** Read the state from the player now. */
  refresh(): Promise<SubtitlesState>;
  /**
   * `role: "secondary"` sets the secondary subtitle: a text track that is not the primary one (`invalid` otherwise). A new source clears it. `track: null` turns the role off.
   */
  select(track: SubtitleTrack | null, options?: SubtitleConditional & {
    role?: "primary" | "secondary";
  }): Promise<SubtitlesState>;
  /**
   * Upload a subtitle file's bytes (UTF-8 SRT, or ASS/SSA with
   * `format: "ass"`) for the current source; select it unless
   * `select: "none"`. `title` (1–200 characters) names the track: data, or
   * a Text the player translates (`text("{} · {}", [text("Simplified
   * Chinese"), file])`, SDK 1.5.11). Aborting
   * `signal` before the commit discards the upload (rejects with AbortError);
   * once the commit was sent it completes.
   *
   * Limits: SRT ≤ 2 MiB and ≤ 10,000 cues; ASS ≤ 2 MiB with `[Script Info]`
   * and `[Events]` and 1–20,000 `Dialogue:` lines. Convert other formats
   * (VTT, SAMI) to SRT first.
   */
  load(bytes: Uint8Array, options?: SubtitleConditional & {
    format?: "srt" | "ass";
    title?: string | Text;
    select?: "primary" | "secondary" | "none";
    signal?: AbortSignal;
  }): Promise<SubtitleTrack>;
  /** Remove a track this plugin loaded. */
  remove(track: SubtitleTrack, options?: SubtitleConditional): Promise<SubtitlesState>;
  /** This plugin's style layer; `null` removes it. Last write wins. */
  setStyle(style: SubtitleStyle | null, options?: SubtitleConditional): Promise<SubtitlesState>;
}
```

### CaptureOptions

Options of MediaCapture.capture. Conditional on `player.state`
like other controls.

```ts
interface CaptureOptions extends Conditional {
  /** Source time; defaults to the current position at the moment of capture. */
  at?: number;
  /** Include this plugin set's effects (and subtitles unless `subtitles: false`). */
  processed?: boolean;
  /** With `processed`, include the primary subtitle (default true). */
  subtitles?: boolean;
  /** Audio to freeze with the snapshot: the selected track, none, or a track id. */
  audio?: "selected" | "none" | number;
}
```

### Snapshot

A frozen, immutable input for exports. Dispose to release it.

```ts
interface Snapshot extends Disposable {
  /** Without or with effects. */
  readonly kind: "raw" | "processed";
  /** Source time in seconds. */
  readonly time: number;
  /** The source path or URL. */
  readonly source: string;
  /** Media duration in seconds (the backend's estimate). */
  readonly duration: number;
  /** The frozen audio track id, `null` for none. */
  readonly audioTrack: number | null;
  /** Processed snapshots: output size and the frozen processing revision. */
  readonly presentation: {
    /** Output width in pixels. */
    width: number;
    /** Output height in pixels. */
    height: number;
  } | null;
  /** The frozen processing revision (processed snapshots). */
  readonly processingRevision: number | null;
  /** Start exporting; the job runs in the host's offline worker. One snapshot can be exported several times. */
  export(options: ExportOptions): Promise<ExportJob>;
}
```

### ExportOptions

One frame as PNG, JPEG (`quality` 1–100, default 90) or BMP (24-bit), or
a clip as MP4.

`destination` is never overwritten if it exists. The extension does not
choose the format. `sampleTime` picks the frame (default: the snapshot
time); `end` is the clip's end in source seconds. On Windows the export
worker needs FFmpeg 6.1 or newer.

```ts
type ExportOptions = {
  /** A lossless frame. */
  format: "png" | "bmp";
  /** Absolute path of the new file. */
  destination: string;
  /** The frame's source time; default the snapshot time. */
  sampleTime?: number;
} | {
  /** A JPEG frame. */
  format: "jpeg";
  /** Absolute path of the new file. */
  destination: string;
  /** The frame's source time; default the snapshot time. */
  sampleTime?: number;
  /** Integer 1–100, default 90. */
  quality?: number;
} | {
  /** A clip from the snapshot time. */
  format: "mp4";
  /** Absolute path of the new file. */
  destination: string;
  /** Clip end, source seconds. */
  end: number;
};
```

### JobState

An export job's state. `status` is `queued`, `running`, `cancelling`,
`completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`; once terminal, `outcome` is
`{ destination }`, `{ error: { code, message } }` or `{ cancelled: true }`.
`facts` describes what the worker produced (versions, range, streams).

```ts
type JobState = Omit<MediaJob, "jobId">;
```

### ExportJob

An export, from Snapshot.export. Disposing an unfinished job cancels it.

```ts
interface ExportJob extends Disposable {
  /** Latest state. */
  readonly state: JobState;
  /** The state changed. */
  onChange(listener: (state: JobState) => void): Disposable;
  /** Resolves with the terminal state (completed, failed or cancelled). */
  readonly done: Promise<JobState>;
  /** Ask to cancel: `requested`, `tooLate` (already publishing) or `terminal` (already over). */
  cancel(): Promise<"requested" | "tooLate" | "terminal">;
  /** Read the state from the player now. */
  refresh(): Promise<JobState>;
}
```

### MediaCapture

`plugin.media`: snapshots and exports. Needs `media.read` and
`media.control` (processed snapshots also `playback.read` and
`subtitles.read`). Exports decode offline and do not disturb playback.

```ts
interface MediaCapture {
  /**
   * Freeze the current source (and optionally this plugin set's effects) as an input for exports. Fails `stale` when the source changed since `ifCurrent`; `unsupported` for an external ASS track with subtitles; `noSource` when nothing is playing.
   */
  capture(options?: CaptureOptions): Promise<Snapshot>;
}
```

### ResolverOptions

Declaration of Resolvers.add: a web resolver
(WebResolverOptions) or a file resolver (FileResolverOptions).

```ts
type ResolverOptions = WebResolverOptions | FileResolverOptions;
```

### WebResolverOptions

A resolver for web pages: `https://host/…` to playable stream URLs.

```ts
interface WebResolverOptions {
  /** Local id, unique within the plugin. */
  id: string;
  /** URL schemes handled. */
  schemes: ("http" | "https")[];
  /** Exact host names. */
  hosts: string[];
  /** Turn a page URL into playable stream URLs. */
  resolve(url: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ResolvedMedia>;
}
```

### FileResolverOptions

A resolver for local files by extension (SDK 1.5.3, player 0.4.1): when
anyone opens such a file with Player.open (the Open dialog, the
playlist, next / previous, the recent list, a drop that calls `open`),
the player asks this plugin for a stream it generates instead of
playing the file. Needs `source.resolve` and `producer.av`.

```ts
interface FileResolverOptions {
  /** Local id, unique within the plugin. */
  id: string;
  /**
   * Lower case, without the dot: 1–16 entries of 1–16 lower-case letters or digits (not `"folder"`). Only absolute local paths match, by their extension in any case (`/roms/Game.NES`); URLs never do.
   */
  extensions: string[];
  /** Read the file and describe the stream to generate for it. */
  resolve(path: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ResolvedStream>;
}
```

### ResolvedStream

What a file resolver returns: a stream, with the same frame contract as
StreamOptions (size limits, `frame()` on the audio clock).

After `resolve` returns, the SDK starts the stream while the open waits.
If that fails, the open fails with the player's words instead of the
SDK's (the detail goes to the log): `device` "音频输出设备不可用",
`timeout` "启动超时", `busy` "播放器正忙，请稍后重试", other start-up
failures "无法启动播放". An error thrown by `frame()` keeps its message.
To give your own text for a file you can tell is unusable (a bad header),
check it in `resolve` and throw there.

```ts
interface ResolvedStream {
  /** Always `"stream"`. */
  kind: "stream";
  /** Frame width in pixels. */
  width: number;
  /** Frame height in pixels. */
  height: number;
  /** Produce the next frame. Never called concurrently or while paused. */
  frame(): StreamFrame;
  /**
   * Called with the running stream once the player plays it, synchronously after activation and before any Stream.onStop. Not called when the open was cancelled first. `stream.stop()` closes the source (if still current); the plugin stopping stops it too.
   */
  started?(stream: Stream): void;
}
```

### Resolver

A registered resolver. Disposing it unregisters it and aborts resolutions in flight.

```ts
interface Resolver extends Disposable {
  /**
   * Resolves when the player registered it; rejects otherwise: `conflict` when another resolver has the extension or the scheme + host (another plugin's: activation goes on; this plugin's own: activation fails), `invalid` for a malformed declaration (a player before 0.4.1 also for `extensions`).
   */
  readonly ready: Promise<void>;
}
```

### Resolvers

`plugin.resolvers`: turn web page URLs into playable streams, or local
files into streams this plugin generates. Needs `source.resolve` (file
resolvers also `producer.av`).

```ts
interface Resolvers {
  /**
   * Register a resolver. When anyone opens a matching URL or file the player calls `resolve`; `signal` aborts when the open is cancelled or replaced. One scheme + host pair, and one extension, has one resolver (`conflict` otherwise). A rejected `resolve` fails the open with the error's message.
   */
  add(options: ResolverOptions): Resolver;
  /**
   * The extensions some plugin's file resolver handles (SDK 1.5.8, player 0.4.2): lower case, without the dot, sorted, each once; not who registered them. Reading needs no capability; `[]` from older players. Without `events` it is the list from when the plugin first read it. Use it to accept such files beside the player's own media types, for example in a playlist's drop or folder scan.
   * @capability None.
   * @player 0.4.2
   */
  readonly fileTypes: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Resolvers.fileTypes changed: a file resolver was added, or its plugin stopped. Needs `events`; without it the listener never fires.
   * @param listener - Receives the new list.
   * @returns A handle that removes the listener.
   * @capability `events`
   * @player 0.4.2
   */
  onFileTypesChange(listener: (types: string[]) => void): Disposable;
}
```

### PackageManifest

The manifest of a package, as validated. The display fields and
`minPlayerVersion` are optional (player 0.2.0); see the API reference for
their rules.

```ts
interface PackageManifest {
  /** Plugin id. */
  id: string;
  /** `x.y.z`. */
  version: string;
  /** `vestra/1`. */
  apiVersion: string;
  /** Entry module path inside the package. */
  entry: string;
  /** Declared capabilities. */
  capabilities: string[];
  /** Display name, 1–64 characters. */
  name?: string;
  /** Author, 1–64 characters. */
  author?: string;
  /** One-line summary, 1–120 characters. */
  punchline?: string;
  /** Plain-text description, 1–2000 characters. */
  description?: string;
  /** Up to 8 tags of 1–24 characters. */
  tags?: string[];
  /** Package path of a PNG or JPEG icon (≤ 512 KB, sides ≤ 1024). */
  icon?: string;
  /** Package path of the README (`.md`, ≤ 256 KB); `README.md` when present. */
  readme?: string;
  /** Package path of the changelog (`.md`, ≤ 256 KB); `CHANGELOG.md` when present. */
  changelog?: string;
  /** `https:` address of the source code. */
  sourceUrl?: string;
  /** License, preferably an SPDX expression. */
  license?: string;
  /** The oldest player version that can load the package (`x.y.z`). */
  minPlayerVersion?: string;
}
```

### PackageSource

Where an installed plugin came from. Installs with the same source
upgrade the plugin and keep its data; links and local files count as one
source. `bundled` marks the player's built-in plugins (set by the player
only).

```ts
type PackageSource = {
  /** A repository. */
  kind: "repository";
  /** The full address of its `index.json`. */
  url: string;
} | {
  /** A package link. */
  kind: "link";
  /** The package's address. */
  url: string;
} | {
  /** A local `.vxp` file or package directory. */
  kind: "file";
} | {
  /** Generated by the plugin workshop. */
  kind: "workshop";
} | {
  /** Shipped with the player (built-in). */
  kind: "bundled";
};
```

### InstallOptions

Options of PackageCandidate.install.

```ts
interface InstallOptions {
  /** Where the package comes from (default `{ kind: "file" }`). Repository and link addresses must be `http(s)`. `bundled` is `invalid`. */
  source?: PackageSource;
  /**
   * Replace a plugin of the same id installed from another source (ask the user first). Without it such an install fails with `conflict`. The replaced plugin's data is kept; installing from its source again reconnects to it.
   */
  replace?: boolean;
}
```

### PackageCandidate

A validated package directory, from Packages.validate.

```ts
interface PackageCandidate {
  /** The package directory. */
  readonly directory: string;
  /** Content digest of the package. */
  readonly digest: string;
  /** Its manifest. */
  readonly manifest: PackageManifest;
  /** The checks the player ran. */
  readonly checks: string[];
  /**
   * Install it. The same source upgrades the installed plugin (its data stays); another source fails with `conflict` unless `replace` is set; a built-in id fails with `unsupported` (built-ins update with the player). A reserved id (`vestra` or `vestra.*`, which every built-in uses) fails with `reserved` (player 0.4.1; already when validated), as only the player installs built-in plugins.
   */
  install(options?: InstallOptions): Promise<PackageChange>;
}
```

### PackageChangeStatus

The progress of an install, rollback or uninstall.

```ts
type PackageChangeStatus = "preparing" | "activating" | "restoring" | "committed" | "cancelled" | "failed" | "failedDegraded" | "tooLate";
```

### PackageChange

An install, rollback or uninstall in progress. The SDK never submits a
change twice: after a lost reply it only queries the same request.

```ts
interface PackageChange {
  /** Current status. */
  readonly status: PackageChangeStatus;
  /** Details for failures, `null` otherwise. */
  readonly message: string | null;
  /** The status changed. */
  onChange(listener: (status: PackageChangeStatus) => void): Disposable;
  /** Resolves with the final status. */
  readonly done: Promise<PackageChangeStatus>;
  /** Ask to cancel (it may be `tooLate`). */
  cancel(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### PluginInfo

One plugin as the player knows it (`packages.list`).

```ts
interface PluginInfo {
  /** Manifest id. */
  id: string;
  /** Version, `null` when unknown. */
  version: string | null;
  /** From the install library, or a `--plugin` development load. */
  origin: "installed" | "development";
  /** Run state. */
  state: "starting" | "running" | "disabled" | "failed" | "stopped";
  /** Why it failed (`state: "failed"`). */
  error: string | null;
  /** Declared capabilities. */
  capabilities: string[];
  /** The package directory (read its `manifest.json` for display fields). */
  directory: string;
  /** The version a rollback would restore, `null` without one. */
  previousVersion: string | null;
  /** Shipped with the player: it can be disabled, not uninstalled or replaced. `false` from players before 0.2.0. */
  builtin: boolean;
  /** Where an installed plugin came from; `null` for development loads. */
  source: PackageSource | null;
  /** Its data directory (`plugin.dataDirectory` of that plugin); `null` when the player has none. The path's layout is not part of the API. */
  dataDirectory: string | null;
  /**
   * What a running plugin was refused because another plugin holds it: a panel position (`slot-occupied`, with `slot`) or the next/previous sequence (`sequence-taken`). Neither fails activation; `error` has the same as text. Empty from players before 0.4.x (after 0.4.0). Always set by the SDK; optional so that code building `PluginInfo` values itself (tests) keeps compiling.
   */
  warnings?: readonly PluginWarning[];
  /**
   * The manifest's display texts in the interface language, translated with that package's catalog; absent from players before 0.4.3 (read `manifest.json` there).
   */
  display?: PluginDisplay;
}
```

### PluginDisplay

PluginInfo.display: a package's `name`, `punchline`,
`description` and `tags` as the player shows them.

```ts
interface PluginDisplay {
  /** `name`, translated; `null` when the manifest has none. */
  readonly name: string | null;
  /** `punchline`, translated; `null` when the manifest has none. */
  readonly punchline: string | null;
  /** `description`, translated; `null` when the manifest has none. */
  readonly description: string | null;
  /** `tags`, each translated. */
  readonly tags: readonly string[];
}
```

### PluginWarning

One refusal in PluginInfo.warnings.

```ts
interface PluginWarning {
  /** `"slot-occupied"`, `"sequence-taken"` or `"resolver-taken"` (player 0.4.1); a newer player may add codes. */
  code: string;
  /** The panel position (`"bottom"`, `"sidebar"`, `"backdrop"`) for `slot-occupied`. */
  slot?: string;
  /** What was taken, for `resolver-taken`: 「文件类型 .nes」 or the `scheme://host` of a web resolver. */
  target?: string;
  /** The manifest id of the plugin holding it (absent for a full sidebar). */
  owner?: string;
}
```

### Packages

`plugin.packages`: the plugins the player knows. `list` and `onChange`
need no capability; everything else needs `plugins.manage`.

```ts
interface Packages {
  /**
   * Validate a package directory (`plugins.manage`). A package whose id is
   * reserved for the built-in plugins (`vestra` or `vestra.*`) fails with
   * `reserved` (player 0.4.1).
   *
   * The player keeps the 32 most recent candidates of all plugins; an
   * older one's `install` fails with `stale` (validate again). Before
   * player 0.4.2 the 33rd validation of a run failed with `busy` instead.
   */
  validate(directory: string): Promise<PackageCandidate>;
  /**
   * Validate a `.vxp` package file (`plugins.manage`, player 0.2.0): the same checks as Packages.validate after unpacking. Check the file's sha256 yourself before calling when you know it. A reserved id fails with `reserved`, as in Packages.validate.
   */
  validateArchive(file: string): Promise<PackageCandidate>;
  /** Restore a plugin's previous version (`plugins.manage`). */
  rollback(id: string): Promise<PackageChange>;
  /** Every plugin: running, installed, and this run's development loads. No capability. */
  list(): Promise<PluginInfo[]>;
  /** The new list after any start, stop, failure, install or uninstall. No capability. */
  onChange(listener: (plugins: PluginInfo[]) => void): Disposable;
  /**
   * Stop or start a plugin (`plugins.manage`). An installed plugin stays disabled across launches; a development load only for this run. `invalid` to disable oneself, `missing` unknown. `busy` while it is being installed.
   */
  setEnabled(id: string, enabled: boolean): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Remove an installed plugin (`plugins.manage`); `removeData` also deletes its data directory, otherwise reinstalling it from the same source reconnects to its data. Its user bindings stay (as orphans). `unsupported` for built-ins and development loads, `missing` unknown, `invalid` for oneself.
   */
  uninstall(id: string, options?: {
    removeData?: boolean;
  }): Promise<PackageChange>;
}
```

### BindingRef

A command: manifest id (`"host"` for the player's own) and command id.

```ts
interface BindingRef {
  /** Manifest id, or `"host"`. */
  plugin: string;
  /** Command id within that plugin. */
  command: string;
}
```

### BindingInfo

One command's bindings, from Bindings.list.

```ts
interface BindingInfo extends BindingRef {
  /** Menu title. */
  title: string;
  /** Menu path as shown; `null` for a command outside the menu. */
  path: string[] | null;
  /**
   * The menu path's keys: the English text menus merge by, the same in every interface language (`["Playback", "Seek", "Back 5 s"]`; a built-in menu by its key, `"Video"`, also when declared as `@video`). `null` for a command outside the menu, and from players before 0.4.3. Find a command by where it is in the menu with this, not with `path`. Always set by `list()`; optional so that test fakes written for older SDKs still type-check.
   */
  key?: string[] | null;
  /** Global, or only while the plugin's panel has focus. */
  scope: "global" | "panel";
  /** The command's own bindings. */
  defaults: string[];
  /** In effect for it: the user's override, else the defaults. */
  current: string[];
  /** The user overrode the defaults. */
  overridden: boolean;
  /** Inputs of `current` another command holds. */
  shadowed: {
    /** The input. */
    input: string;
    /** The command that holds it. */
    by: BindingRef;
  }[];
  /** Menu text of each of `current` (`Ctrl+←`, `Num5`). */
  labels: string[];
}
```

### Bindings

`plugin.bindings`: list and override every command's bindings, including
the player's. Needs `bindings.manage`.

```ts
interface Bindings {
  /** Every declared command, and overrides whose command is gone. */
  list(): Promise<{
    /** Every declared command (running plugins and the player). */
    commands: BindingInfo[];
    /** Overrides whose command is not declared now (plugin stopped or removed). */
    orphans: {
      /** The command the override is for. */
      ref: BindingRef;
      /** The saved inputs. */
      inputs: string[];
    }[];
  }>;
  /**
   * Override a command's bindings (`[]` unbinds it); saved across launches. `invalid` for a bad binding, `missing` for an unknown command that has no override either. At most 16 inputs, syntax as CommandOptions.bindings.
   */
  set(ref: BindingRef, inputs: string[]): Promise<void>;
  /** Back to the defaults: one command, or every override when omitted. */
  reset(ref?: BindingRef): Promise<void>;
  /** Declarations or overrides changed (read `list()` again). At most every 200 ms. */
  onChange(listener: () => void): Disposable;
}
```

### Clipboard

The system clipboard (`clipboard`). Unavailable without a user interface.

Platforms: macOS writes text as UTF-8 and images as their original
PNG/JPEG bytes; Windows writes Unicode text and images as a bitmap plus
PNG. Other systems: `unsupported`. Failures: `invalid`, `missing`,
`unavailable`, `failed` (the system refused).

```ts
interface Clipboard {
  /** Plain text on the clipboard; `null` when it holds none. */
  readText(): Promise<string | null>;
  /** Replace the clipboard with text (at most 1 MiB of UTF-8). */
  writeText(text: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Replace the clipboard with a PNG or JPEG file (absolute path, at most 16 MB). */
  writeImage(path: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Power

Keeping the computer awake (`playback.control`).

```ts
interface Power {
  /**
   * `"playing"`: while a source is ready and not paused, keep the display
   * (video) or the system (audio only) from sleeping. Any plugin asking is
   * enough; a stopped plugin's request is withdrawn.
   *
   * It only registers the request (`invalid` for a bad mode); failures to
   * take the system assertion are logged by the player, not reported.
   * macOS uses `caffeinate`, Windows the thread execution state; elsewhere
   * it has no effect.
   */
  preventSleep(mode: "off" | "playing"): Promise<void>;
}
```

### ToolResult

The output of Tools.run.

```ts
interface ToolResult {
  /** Standard output (at most `maxOutput` bytes). */
  stdout: Uint8Array;
  /** The last 64 KiB of standard error. */
  stderr: string;
}
```

### Tools

`plugin.tools`: ffmpeg and ffprobe, run in this plugin's process. No
capability.

```ts
interface Tools {
  /**
   * Run ffmpeg or ffprobe (found through `VESTRA_FFMPEG` / `VESTRA_FFPROBE`,
   * then `PATH`) without a shell. Rejects `unavailable` (not found), `timeout`,
   * `failed` (non-zero exit; `message` is the last stderr line), `invalid`
   * (output over `maxOutput`, default 16 MiB), `aborted` (`signal`). Timeout,
   * `signal` and disposing the scope end the process.
   *
   * Arguments are passed as-is (no quoting needed). On Windows `PATHEXT` is
   * honoured. Ending sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 300 ms (immediate on
   * Windows).
   */
  run(tool: "ffmpeg" | "ffprobe", args: string[], options: {
    timeoutMs: number;
    maxOutput?: number;
    signal?: AbortSignal;
  }): Promise<ToolResult>;
  /** Whether the tool can be found. */
  available(tool: "ffmpeg" | "ffprobe"): Promise<boolean>;
}
```

### JsonStore

A JSON file `dataDirectory/<name>.json`, loaded once and saved debounced.

```ts
interface JsonStore<T> extends Disposable {
  /** The loaded value, or `defaults` when the file was missing or broken. */
  readonly value: T;
  /** Replace the value now and write it after `debounceMs`. Only `save` writes: mutating `value` in place is not saved. */
  save(next: T): void;
  /** Write a pending save now. */
  flush(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Storage

`plugin.storage`: JSON settings files. No capability.

```ts
interface Storage {
  /**
   * Open `<name>.json` (`name`: 1–64 of `a-z 0-9 -`). A file that cannot be
   * parsed or fails `validate` is renamed `<name>.json.bad-<timestamp>` and
   * `defaults` is used. Writes go to a temporary file, then a rename. Disposal
   * (and stopping the plugin) flushes first.
   *
   * The file is read synchronously on creation; `debounceMs` defaults to
   * 300. Files are created with mode 0600. `invalid` for a bad name.
   */
  json<T>(name: string, options: {
    defaults: T;
    validate?: (value: unknown) => value is T;
    debounceMs?: number;
  }): JsonStore<T>;
}
```

### System

`plugin.system`: files and links, executed by the player. No capability.
Other systems than macOS and Windows: `unsupported`.

```ts
interface System {
  /**
   * Select files or folders in the file manager (macOS: one Finder window for all, so several files of one folder are all highlighted; Windows: one Explorer window per folder, selecting its first path). Paths that do not exist are skipped; `missing` when none exists; at most 256.
   */
  reveal(paths: string | string[]): Promise<void>;
  /** Open the file or folder with its default application. `missing` if absent. */
  openPath(path: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Open an http(s) address in the default browser. `invalid` for another protocol or a malformed address; `timeout` after 10 s, `failed` otherwise. */
  openUrl(url: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Secrets

Per-plugin secrets (API keys, passwords) in the system's secret store:
the login keychain on macOS, the Credential Manager on Windows. Needs
`secrets`. `unsupported` on systems without a store, `unavailable` when
the store refuses access: keep a fallback (or ask again).

The user denying access and other system errors reject `failed`. Never
write secrets to settings files.

```ts
interface Secrets {
  /** The stored value, `null` when there is none. */
  get(name: string): Promise<string | null>;
  /**
   * Store or replace (`name`: 1–64 of `a-z 0-9 . _ -`; value 1–1024 bytes). At most 256 different names per plugin: a new name beyond that rejects `limit`. Uninstalling with `removeData` deletes them.
   */
  set(name: string, value: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Remove; removing a missing secret is fine. */
  delete(name: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

### VideoNode

One node of a VideoFilter chain, by `kind`. Values outside the
ranges below fail with `invalid`. Fields marked "live" change in place
while playing; changing any other field rebuilds the stage (the picture
may stall for one frame), so drive sliders with live fields.

Nodes act after the player's own orientation handling (container
rotation): a portrait video is upright before `transform` runs. At most
64 nodes across all plugins.

```ts
type VideoNode = 
/** FFmpeg `eq`; every field is live. */
{
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "eq";
  /** −1–1, 0 = unchanged. */
  brightness: number;
  /** 0–2, 1 = unchanged. */
  contrast: number;
  /** 0–2, 1 = unchanged. */
  saturation: number;
  /** 0.5–2, 1 = unchanged. */
  gamma: number;
}
/** Gaussian blur (FFmpeg `gblur`). */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "gblur";
  /** 0–10 (live). */
  sigma: number;
  /** Always 3. */
  steps: 3;
}
/** Hue rotation; changes in place while playing. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "hue";
  /** −180–180 (live). */
  degrees: number;
}
/** unsharp: 3×3 (`small`) or 7×7 (`large`) luma matrix. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "sharpen";
  /** 0–2. */
  amount: number;
  /** Matrix size. */
  size: "small" | "large";
}
/** hqdn3d strengths. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "denoise";
  /** 0–20 (0 = off). */
  lumaSpatial: number;
  /** 0–20 (0 = off). */
  chromaSpatial: number;
  /** 0–20 (0 = off). */
  lumaTemporal: number;
  /** 0–20 (0 = off). */
  chromaTemporal: number;
}
/** FFmpeg `deblock`. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "deblock";
  /** Filter strength. */
  strength: "weak" | "strong";
}
/** FFmpeg `deband`. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "deband";
  /** 0.003–0.5, the same for all four planes. */
  threshold: number;
  /** Integer 1–64. */
  range: number;
}
/** Applied after the player's own source orientation. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "transform";
  /** Clockwise degrees; applied before the flips. */
  rotate: 0 | 90 | 180 | 270;
  /** Mirror horizontally. */
  flipH: boolean;
  /** Mirror vertically. */
  flipV: boolean;
}
/** BWDIF; `field` doubles the frame rate. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "deinterlace";
  /** `interlaced`: only frames flagged interlaced; `all`: every frame. */
  when: "interlaced" | "all";
  /** One frame per frame, or one per field (double rate). */
  output: "frame" | "field";
}
/** Crop to / pad to a display aspect; x, y place it (−1 left/top … 1 right/bottom). */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "reframe";
  /** Crop the picture, or pad it with black bars. */
  mode: "crop" | "pad";
  /** Target display aspect 0.25–4. */
  aspect: number;
  /** −1 (left) … 0 (centre) … 1 (right). */
  x: number;
  /** −1 (top) … 0 (centre) … 1 (bottom). */
  y: number;
}
/** Blended frame-rate conversion (FFmpeg `framerate`), an integer 24–120. At most one across all plugins; the player runs it after every chain. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "frameBlend";
  /** Output frame rate, integer 24–120. */
  fps: number;
};
```

### AudioNode

One node of an AudioFilter chain, by `kind`. Values outside the
ranges fail with `invalid`; "live" fields change in place while playing.

```ts
type AudioNode = 
/** FFmpeg `volume`. */
{
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "volume";
  /** −60–0 dB (live). */
  gainDb: number;
}
/** One peaking equalizer band (FFmpeg `equalizer`). */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "equalizer";
  /** Centre frequency 20–20000 Hz. */
  frequency: number;
  /** Always 1. */
  q: 1;
  /** −6–6 dB (live). */
  gainDb: number;
}
/** Treble shelf (FFmpeg `treble`). */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "treble";
  /** Always 3000 Hz. */
  frequency: 3000;
  /** Always 0.5. */
  slope: 0.5;
  /** 0–6 dB (live). */
  gainDb: number;
}
/** Dynamic loudness normalization (FFmpeg `dynaudnorm`); every field is live. */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "dynaudnorm";
  /** On or off. */
  enabled: boolean;
  /** Maximum gain 1–4. */
  maxGain: number;
  /** Target peak 0.5–0.95. */
  peak: number;
}
/** Routing on a stereo mix (more channels are mixed down first). */
 | {
  /** The node type. */
  kind: "channels";
  /** `stereo` leaves it unchanged. */
  mode: "stereo" | "left" | "right" | "mono" | "swap";
};
```

### ResolvedMedia

What a resolver returns (WebResolverOptions.resolve): the playable
stream(s) behind a page URL. Both streams must use identical `headers`;
different maps fail explicitly (nothing is dropped silently).

```ts
type ResolvedMedia = {
  /** Always `"media"`. */
  kind: "media";
  /** The page URL that was resolved. */
  originalUrl: string;
  /** A title for the player to show. */
  title?: string;
  /** The video (or combined) stream. */
  primary: ResolvedResource;
  /** A separate audio stream, when audio and video are split. */
  audio?: ResolvedResource;
};
```

### SubtitleStyle

A subtitle style layer (Subtitles.setStyle). Sizes are at the
1080p reference height and scale with the video. The effective style is
the layer of the plugin that set one last; it also applies to the
secondary subtitle.

```ts
type SubtitleStyle = {
  /** A font id from SubtitlesState.fonts. */
  fontId: string;
  /** 16–72. */
  fontSize: number;
  /** Text colour. */
  color: "white" | "yellow" | "cyan";
  /** Outline width 0–4. */
  outline: number;
  /** Bottom margin 2–15 % of the video height. */
  marginPercent: number;
  /** Timing offset −600000–600000 ms. */
  offsetMs: number;
  /** Bold text; default false. */
  bold?: boolean;
  /** Shadow offset 0–4 at the 1080p reference height. */
  shadow?: number;
  /** Background box opacity 0–100; `null` or omitted: no box (the shadow applies). */
  box?: number | null;
  /** `keep` (default): ASS scripts keep their own styling; `force`: this style replaces it. */
  assOverride?: "keep" | "force";
  /** Where the secondary subtitle sits; default `top`. */
  secondaryPosition?: "top" | "aboveMain";
};
```

### Json

A JSON value: what crosses the wire to the player. Slint property values,
callback arguments and protocol parameters are all `Json`.

```ts
type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | {
  [key: string]: Json;
};
```

## API: @vestra-player/sdk/testing

Test tools for Vestra Player plugins: an in-memory fake player
(TestHost) and startPlugin, which activates a plugin against
it.

`TestHost` speaks the real wire protocol, so the SDK's own logic (revisions,
conditional commits, recovery after lost replies, coalescing of updates)
runs exactly as it does inside the player. Only the player side is faked,
and its semantics are simplified:

- no media decoding: sources are facts you set with
  TestHost.setSource or TestHost.openElsewhere;
- no Slint and no native windows: views are records of their properties
  and callbacks (FakeWindow), and you fire callbacks yourself;
- export jobs advance one step on every state query
  (`queued` → `running` → `completed`);
- video and audio processing nodes are validated with the player's own
  value ranges (an out-of-range `filter.set` ends in `failed` with
  `invalid`), an empty chain removes the plugin's chain, a chain on a
  generated stream fails `unsupported` (the player's own conformance
  cases check all three), and the command limits (COMMAND_LIMITS),
  property value limits (UI_VALUE_LIMITS) and menu ids
  (MENU_IDS) are enforced.

Typical workflow: start the plugin with startPlugin (it reads the
plugin's `manifest.json`), drive it the way the user or another plugin
would (run commands, press bindings, fire view callbacks, change the
source), wait with TestHost.settle, assert on what the host
recorded (`host.osd`, `host.window(id).props`, `host.sent(method)`, …), and
finally call `stop()`.

Use it from `node:test` (what `vestra-plugin test` runs). Each test should
create its own host; `stop()` removes the host's temporary directories.

### FakeWindow

A tool window as the test host keeps it: the record of a
`plugin.windows.create(...)` window after its first `show()`. Get one with
TestHost.window.

```ts
interface FakeWindow {
  /** The `.slint` file the window was created from (package-relative). */
  file: string;
  /** Whether the window is shown (`show()`) or hidden (`hide()`). */
  visible: boolean;
  /**
   * The properties the plugin wrote, by their Slint (kebab-case) names: `canMark` is stored as `can-mark`. Runtime images appear in their wire form; read the path with TestHost.imagePath.
   */
  props: Record<string, Json>;
  /** The Slint callback names (kebab-case) the plugin bound with `on()`. */
  callbacks: string[];
  /**
   * Fire a Slint callback as if the user triggered it in the window. The name may be kebab-case or camelCase; `args` are the callback arguments. Follow it with `await host.settle()` before asserting.
   */
  emit(callback: string, ...args: Json[]): void;
  /**
   * The user closes the window with its title-bar button: the window closes and the plugin's `window.onClose` listeners run (unlike the plugin's own `close()`).
   */
  userClose(): void;
}
```

### FileDialogText

A file dialog as the player shows it (TestHost.fileDialogs).

```ts
interface FileDialogText {
  /** Which dialog. */
  kind: "openFile" | "openFiles" | "openDirectory" | "saveFile";
  /** Its title as shown, if the plugin gave one. */
  title?: string;
  /** The proposed file name as shown, if the plugin gave one. */
  fileName?: string;
}
```

### FakeCommand

A command the plugin registered with `plugin.commands.add`, as the test
host keeps it. Get one with TestHost.command (the plugin's own) or
TestHost.coreAction (the player's core actions).

```ts
interface FakeCommand {
  /** What the plugin declared: id, menu path, title, order, group, default bindings, focus and repeat. Wire-level shape; it may gain fields in minor versions. */
  declaration: CommandDeclaration;
  /**
   * What the menu shows, as the player shows it in the test host's TestHost.locale: the title and each path segment translated with the plugin's catalog (the player's own menus in the player's words), the keys normalized (`@video` is "Video").
   */
  readonly display: {
    /** The menu text of the item. */
    title: string;
    /** Each segment of the path as shown; empty without a path. */
    path: string[];
    /**
     * The disabled or busy reason as shown, `null` without one (a plugin command's; not enumerable, so comparing `display` with `{ title, path }` still works).
     */
    reason?: string | null;
  };
  /** The command state the player last received (after the update pass). */
  state: {
    /** `false` when the plugin disabled the command. */
    enabled: boolean;
    /** The check mark: `true`, `false`, or `null` for none. */
    checked: boolean | null;
    /** `true` while the plugin reports the command as busy. */
    busy: boolean;
    /** The reason the plugin sent (source text or a text value; see `display.reason`). */
    reason: TextValue | null;
  };
  /** The state revision the player holds; increases with every state update the SDK sends. */
  revision: number;
  /**
   * Execute the command the way the menu would, then wait until the host is idle. Rejects (with a HostError) when the command is disabled or busy, like the player, which does not call `run` then.
   */
  run(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### FakeProducer

A generated stream (`plugin.player.openStream`) as the test host sees it:
the fake player end of the frame connection. Assertion surface; see
TestHost.producers.

```ts
interface FakeProducer {
  /** The producer id the host assigned (`1`, `2`, … per host). */
  id: number;
  /** Audio sample frames received so far (one stereo f32 pair = 1 frame). */
  receivedFrames: number;
  /** Video frames received so far. */
  videoFrames: number;
  /** `true` once the plugin released the producer (stream stopped or disposed). */
  released: boolean;
  /**
   * `true` once the player retired the producer, as the real player does at once: another source replaced it (`open`, another stream, a resolved file), the source was closed, or TestHost.failStream failed it. A retired producer's `producer.state` answers `unavailable`.
   */
  retired: boolean;
  /**
   * `true` if the frame connection closed while this stream was still the player's source: the player reports that as a playback failure ("producer transport closed"). `stop()` closes the source first.
   */
  droppedWhileSelected: boolean;
}
```

### MarkdownWire

A Markdown document as TestHost.markdown reads it back.

```ts
interface MarkdownWire {
  /** The Markdown text. */
  text: string;
  /** The base given to `ui.markdown`, or `null`. */
  base: string | null;
  /** Remote image address → the file the SDK downloaded for it. */
  images: Record<string, string>;
}
```

### TestHost

An in-memory fake Vestra Player for plugin tests.

The plugin under test talks to it over the real wire protocol (the host is
the plugin's transport), so everything the SDK does runs unchanged. The
host answers each request with simplified player behaviour, records what
the plugin did, and lets the test act as the user or another plugin.

Members fall into a few groups:

- **Drive the plugin**: TestHost.command`(id).run()`,
  TestHost.press, TestHost.window`(id).emit(...)`,
  TestHost.mounted`().emit(...)`, TestHost.drop,
  TestHost.step, TestHost.dialogAnswers.
- **Simulate the player and other plugins**: TestHost.setSource,
  TestHost.openElsewhere, TestHost.setMainWindow,
  TestHost.setTimelineLayer, TestHost.setAppearance,
  TestHost.setPackages, TestHost.emit.
- **Preset data** the plugin reads: TestHost.stats,
  TestHost.app, TestHost.systemInfo,
  TestHost.chapters, TestHost.audioDevices,
  TestHost.secrets, TestHost.clipboard,
  TestHost.tools.
- **Assert** on records: TestHost.osd, TestHost.calls,
  TestHost.sent, TestHost.conflicts,
  TestHost.layout, TestHost.menus, and many more.
- **Inject failures**: TestHost.handle / TestHost.reset.
- **Synchronise**: TestHost.settle.

Usually created by startPlugin. Create one yourself only to preset
data that the plugin reads during activation (`app`, `appearance`,
`secrets`, ...), then pass it as `startPlugin(activate, { host })`.

Fields that mirror player state at the wire level (`source`, `subtitles`,
`processing`, `snapshots`, `jobs`, `producers`, `uploads`, `resolvers`,
`calls`) use the protocol's shapes. They are fine for assertions but are
not part of the plugin API: their shape may change in minor versions.

```ts
class TestHost implements Transport {
  /** Every request the plugin sent, in order: `{ method, params }`. Wire-level; prefer TestHost.sent for one method. */
  readonly calls: Call[];
  /** The host events the plugin subscribed to (needs `events` etc.). */
  readonly subscriptions: Set<string>;
  /**
   * The player's source facts (phase, position, duration, paused, rate, audio tracks, loop, ...). Wire-level shape; change it with TestHost.setSource, which also broadcasts it.
   */
  source: SourceState;
  /** Tool windows by id (see TestHost.window). */
  readonly windows: Map<string, FakeWindow>;
  /** The plugin's mounted panel (bottom bar, sidebar or backdrop), or `null`. See TestHost.mounted. */
  panel: (Omit<FakeWindow, "callbacks" | "userClose"> & {
    /** `"bottom"`, `"sidebar"` or `"backdrop"`. */
    slot: string;
    /** The exported component the SDK found in the file. */
    component: string;
    /** The last `panel.setInteraction(...)` locks, `null` before any. */
    locks: Json;
  }) | null;
  /** The plugin's commands by local id (see TestHost.command). */
  readonly commands: Map<string, FakeCommand>;
  /** The player's 14 core actions (`host/<id>`), kept apart from the plugin's `commands`. */
  readonly coreCommands: Map<string, FakeCommand>;
  /**
   * Both panel positions as the player reports them (`null` while no panel is mounted there). You may change a slot directly and then call `host.emit("window.state", {})` to simulate a change made elsewhere.
   */
  readonly layout: {
    /** The bottom bar position: `preferred`, `effective`, `reason`, `detached`, `owner` and `panels` (its one panel). */
    bottom: LayoutSlot | null;
    /**
     * The sidebar position: `preferred`, `effective`, `reason`, `detached`; `panels` are its tabs in order (`{ owner, plugin, title }`), `owner` the current tab's (the plugin under test is owner 1).
     */
    sidebar: LayoutSlot | null;
  };
  /**
   * Every `osd.show` text as the player shows it (translated with the plugin's catalog and formatted with its args), newest last. The template and args the plugin sent are in `host.sent("osd.show")`.
   */
  readonly osd: string[];
  /** The text of this plugin's osd panel as shown, `null` when hidden. */
  osdPanel: string | null;
  /**
   * The interface language the test host plays (`plugin.i18n.locale`), `"en"`
   * by default. Set it before startPlugin (or pass its `locale`
   * option): the plugin's catalog for it is read from the package's
   * `locales/` then, and the menus (FakeCommand.display), OSD
   * messages, dialog texts, settings page and panel titles show its
   * translations, the way the player shows them.
   *
   * The player's own texts (core actions' messages and menus, its
   * refusals) are English, or the player's Simplified Chinese for
   * `"zh-Hans"`. While `locale` was never set they stay in Chinese, as
   * players up to 0.4.2 showed them, so tests written for SDK 1.5.8 keep
   * passing; set `locale` to test what a user sees now.
   */
  get locale(): Locale;
  set locale(locale: Locale);
  /**
   * Read the plugin's translations for TestHost.locale from a package directory, as the player would (`locales/<locale>.json` of a built package, else the source `locales/<locale>.po`); `startPlugin` does this. None for English; a missing file means none; a broken `.po` throws.
   * @param directory - The package directory (holding `locales/`).
   */
  loadCatalog(directory: string): void;
  /**
   * A text of the plugin as the player shows it: translated with the plugin's catalog (TestHost.loadCatalog), then formatted with `args` when given.
   * @param text - English source text or template.
   * @param args - Values for its placeholders.
   * @returns The shown text.
   */
  translate(text: TextValue, args?: TemplateArgs): string;
  /** The saved interface language (`plugin.appearance.language`), changed by `appearance.setLanguage` or TestHost.setLanguage. */
  language: LanguagePreference;
  /**
   * Simulate another plugin (or the user) saving the interface language: pushes `appearance.changed`.
   * @param language - `"system"` or a locale.
   */
  setLanguage(language: LanguagePreference): void;
  /**
   * Every `dialogs.confirm` as the player shows it: its texts translated (message and detail formatted with `args`), newest last. The options the plugin sent are in TestHost.confirms.
   */
  readonly confirmTexts: {
    /** The question. */
    message: string;
    /** The text under it, if any. */
    detail?: string;
    /** The confirm button. */
    confirm: string;
    /** The cancel button (the player's "Cancel" by default). */
    cancel: string;
    /** The checkbox, if any. */
    checkbox?: string;
  }[];
  /**
   * Every file dialog (`openFile`, `openFiles`, `openDirectory`, `saveFile`) as the player shows it: the title translated, a text file name translated, newest last. The options the plugin sent are in `host.sent("dialogs.open")`.
   */
  readonly fileDialogs: FileDialogText[];
  /** The sequence provider's flags, `null` without a provider. */
  sequence: {
    /** The provider's `canNext`, as last evaluated. */
    canNext: boolean;
    /** The provider's `canPrevious`, as last evaluated. */
    canPrevious: boolean;
  } | null;
  /** What `player.stats()` returns. Fields added in later rounds may be left out; the SDK fills them with `null`. */
  stats: PlaybackStats;
  /** Every `subtitles.load`: its options and bytes, newest last. */
  readonly subtitleLoads: {
    /** The `format` option (`"srt"` by default). */
    format: "srt" | "ass";
    /** The `title` option, `null` when omitted. */
    title: string | null;
    /** The `select` option (`"primary"` by default). */
    select: "primary" | "secondary" | "none";
    /** The uploaded file bytes. */
    bytes: Buffer;
  }[];
  /** The fake system clipboard. Preset `text` to test `readText`; `writeText` replaces it and `writeImage` appends the image path. */
  readonly clipboard: {
    /** The clipboard's text, `null` when it holds none. */
    text: string | null;
    /** Paths given to `clipboard.writeImage`, newest last. */
    images: string[];
  };
  /** The effective `power.preventSleep` mode. */
  power: "off" | "playing";
  /** The fake `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe` behind `plugin.tools`. A tool without a handler is not found (`available()` is false, `run()` rejects with `unavailable`). */
  readonly tools: {
    /** Every run: the tool name and its arguments, newest last. */
    calls: {
      /** `"ffmpeg"` or `"ffprobe"`. */
      tool: string;
      /** The arguments, as passed to `tools.run`. */
      args: string[];
    }[];
    /** @internal The installed handlers by tool; use `handle()`. */
    handlers: Map<string, (args: string[]) => {
      stdout?: Uint8Array | string;
      stderr?: string;
    } | Promise<{
      stdout?: Uint8Array | string;
      stderr?: string;
    }>>;
    /**
     * Make `tool` available and answer each run with `handler(args)`. Return `{ stdout?, stderr? }` (a string `stdout` is UTF-8 encoded), or throw a HostError to fail the run with that code. A later call replaces the handler.
     */
    handle(tool: "ffmpeg" | "ffprobe", handler: (args: string[]) => {
      stdout?: Uint8Array | string;
      stderr?: string;
    } | Promise<{
      stdout?: Uint8Array | string;
      stderr?: string;
    }>): void;
  };
  /** Paths given to `system.reveal` / `system.openPath`, newest last; inject failures with `host.handle("system.openPath", …)`. */
  readonly system: {
    /** Paths given to `system.reveal`, newest last. */
    revealed: string[];
    /** Paths given to `system.openPath`, newest last. */
    opened: string[];
    /** `system.openUrl` addresses, newest last. */
    urls: string[];
  };
  /** Every `panel.showMenu`, newest last. */
  readonly menus: {
    /** Command ids, `null` for a separator. */
    items: (string | null)[];
    /** `at.x`, in window coordinates. */
    x: number;
    /** `at.y`, in window coordinates. */
    y: number;
  }[];
  /** Timeline layers by plugin id (this plugin's is `manifestId`) and the merged list `plugin.timeline.marks` reads. A new source clears them. */
  readonly timeline: {
    /** Each plugin's layer by plugin id; layers with no marks are absent. */
    layers: Map<string, {
      /** Seconds from the start. */
      time: number;
      /** `"chapter"`, `"bookmark"` or `"marker"`. */
      kind: string;
      /** The mark's title, `null` without one. */
      title: string | null;
    }[]>;
    /** Every layer merged, sorted by time, with the publishing plugin's id. */
    readonly marks: {
      /** The manifest id of the plugin that published the mark. */
      plugin: string;
      /** Seconds from the start. */
      time: number;
      /** `"chapter"`, `"bookmark"` or `"marker"`. */
      kind: string;
      /** The mark's title, `null` without one. */
      title: string | null;
    }[];
  };
  /**
   * Simulate another plugin publishing its timeline layer (or clearing it with `[]`); pushes `timeline.changed` when the plugin subscribed.
   * @param pluginId - The other plugin's manifest id.
   * @param marks - Its whole layer.
   */
  setTimelineLayer(pluginId: string, marks: {
    time: number;
    kind: string;
    title?: string | null;
  }[]): void;
  /** Runtime images written to views (`plugin.ui.image`), newest last. The SDK refuses images of released scopes before anything is sent. */
  readonly images: {
    /** The image file's path, as given to `ui.image`. */
    path: string;
    /** The SDK's reference number for that `ImageRef`. */
    ref: number;
  }[];
  /**
   * The file an image property shows, or `null` when the value is not a runtime image. View properties hold images in their wire form; this reads the path back.
   */
  imagePath(value: Json | undefined): string | null;
  /** `drops.provide` registrations of this plugin, in order (`id` is the SDK's). */
  readonly dropProviders: {
    /** The SDK's provider id. */
    id: string;
    /** The extensions it takes (lower case, `"folder"` for directories). */
    extensions: string[];
  }[];
  /** The panel has an `onDrop` listener. */
  panelDrops: boolean;
  /**
   * Drop files like the player: on a panel with an `onDrop` listener the whole list goes there; otherwise (and on the video area) grouped by extension to the first provider (`folder` for existing directories). Files nobody takes are ignored. Resolves once the host is idle again.
   * @param paths - The dropped paths, in the order the file manager gives.
   * @param options - `target`: `"video"` (default) or `"panel"`; `at`: the drop point in panel coordinates (default `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); `modifiers`: keys held (default all `false`).
   */
  drop(paths: string[], options?: {
    target?: "video" | "panel";
    at?: {
      x: number;
      y: number;
    };
    modifiers?: Partial<{
      alt: boolean;
      shift: boolean;
      cmd: boolean;
    }>;
  }): Promise<void>;
  /** The palette (`plugin.appearance.theme`); `setAppearance` changes it elsewhere. */
  appearance: ThemeId;
  /** Simulate another plugin switching the palette: updates TestHost.appearance and pushes `appearance.changed`. */
  setAppearance(theme: ThemeId): void;
  /** Settings pages by id (`plugin.settings.page`), every `show` (page id or null), and the page the options window shows. */
  readonly settings: {
    /** Registered pages by page id. */
    pages: Map<string, {
      /** The page's settings category. */
      category: string;
      /** The page title. */
      title: string;
      /** The page order within its category. */
      order: number;
      /** The `.slint` file (package-relative). */
      file: string;
      /** The exported component the SDK found. */
      component: string;
      /** The exported global (the page's bridge) the SDK found. */
      global: string;
      /** The page's properties by Slint (kebab-case) name. */
      props: Record<string, Json>;
      /** Fire one of the page's callbacks. */
      emit(callback: string, ...args: Json[]): void;
    }>;
    /** Every `settings.show(pageId)`: the page id, `null` when omitted. */
    shows: (string | null)[];
    /** The page the options window shows, `null` before any `show`. */
    current: string | null;
    /** Whether the options window is open. */
    open: boolean;
  };
  /** One settings page by id. Throws when it was never registered. */
  settingsPage(id: string): {
    /** The page's settings category. */
    category: string;
    /** The page title. */
    title: string;
    /** The page order within its category. */
    order: number;
    /** The `.slint` file (package-relative). */
    file: string;
    /** The exported component the SDK found. */
    component: string;
    /** The exported global (the page's bridge) the SDK found. */
    global: string;
    /** The page's properties by Slint (kebab-case) name. */
    props: Record<string, Json>;
    /** Fire one of the page's callbacks. */
    emit(callback: string, ...args: Json[]): void;
  };
  /** The backdrop: who mounted it and whether it shows (`panels.backdrop.state`). */
  backdrop: {
    /** The manifest id of the plugin that mounted it. */
    owner: string;
    /** Whether it shows now (no video frame). `true` when mounted. */
    effective: boolean;
  } | null;
  /** Simulate the backdrop's `effective` changing (`false`: a video frame appeared; `true`: there is none again); pushed to the plugin. */
  setBackdropEffective(effective: boolean): void;
  /**
   * Simulate another plugin mounting a panel, before or after the plugin under test, as the player handles it: in the sidebar it is another tab (after the existing ones; the first panel's tab is current); the bottom bar and the backdrop take one panel, so the plugin's own mount there then rejects with `conflict` (not an activation failure, as in the player). Pushed as a `window.state` change.
   * @param slot - The position.
   * @param plugin - The other plugin's manifest id.
   * @param options - `title`: its tab label (default: `plugin`).
   */
  mountOther(slot: "bottom" | "sidebar" | "backdrop", plugin: string, options?: {
    title?: string;
  }): void;
  /** Simulate another plugin's panel going away (TestHost.mountOther): when its tab was current, the next tab (else the previous one) is. */
  unmountOther(plugin: string): void;
  /**
   * Simulate the user clicking a sidebar tab: `plugin`'s panel (the plugin under test's `manifestId`, or one of TestHost.mountOther) becomes the current tab. Pushed as a `window.state` change.
   */
  selectTab(plugin: string): void;
  /** The display layer (`plugin.video.view()`): who owns it (this plugin is `manifestId`) and the values the player holds. */
  readonly videoView: {
    /** The owning plugin's manifest id, `null` while nobody owns it. */
    owner: string | null;
    /** The values the player holds. */
    values: ViewSettings;
  };
  /**
   * Simulate another plugin taking the display layer first (the plugin's `video.view()` then fails with `conflict`), or, with `null`, releasing it (values reset to the defaults).
   */
  setVideoViewOwner(pluginId: string | null): void;
  /**
   * The render options (`plugin.video.render()`): who owns them, the values the player holds, and whether it renders on the GPU (`gpu: false` is software rendering, where every `set` fails with `unsupported`).
   */
  readonly videoRender: {
    /** The owning plugin's manifest id, `null` while nobody owns them. */
    owner: string | null;
    /** The values the player holds. */
    values: RenderSettings;
    /** `true`: GPU rendering; `false`: software rendering (`unsupported`). */
    gpu: boolean;
  };
  /**
   * Simulate another plugin owning the render options (the plugin's `video.render()` then fails with `conflict`), or, with `null`, releasing them (values reset to the defaults).
   */
  setVideoRenderOwner(pluginId: string | null): void;
  /**
   * What the player pushes when mpv cannot compile a shader (code `failed`) or switches to software rendering (`unsupported`, which also sets `videoRender.gpu` to false). Pushed only when this plugin is the owner.
   */
  failVideoRender(code: "failed" | "unsupported", message: string): void;
  /**
   * The player's processing (filter) state. Wire-level; may change in minor versions. `resources` holds each `video.filter` / `audio.filter` chain the plugin applied, keyed by the SDK's resource id.
   */
  readonly processing: {
    /** Increases with every accepted change. */
    configurationRevision: number;
    /** Set a stage here to simulate a blocked backend (`backend-uncertain`). */
    backendUncertain: Partial<Record<"video" | "audio", string>>;
    /** Applied chains by resource id; an empty chain removes its entry, as in the player. */
    resources: Map<string, {
      /** `"video"` or `"audio"`. */
      stage: string;
      /** The chain's revision. */
      revision: number;
      /** The applied nodes. */
      nodes: Json;
      /** The audio delay in milliseconds (audio chains only). */
      offsetMs?: number;
    }>;
    /** Outcomes of processing operations, for the SDK's recovery queries. */
    book: Map<string, {
      /** The operation's outcome. */
      status: "completed" | "failed";
      /** The result of a completed operation. */
      result?: Json;
      /** The refusal of a failed operation. */
      error?: {
        /** The error code. */
        code: string;
        /** The error message. */
        message: string;
      };
    }>;
  };
  /**
   * The player's subtitle state: tracks, selection, style layers, fonts and loaded resources. Wire-level shape (may change in minor versions); add tracks to `subtitles.tracks` (entries may carry `codec`, `text`, `streamIndex`) to simulate a source's subtitles.
   */
  subtitles: SubtitleState;
  /** Subtitle uploads in progress, by upload id. Wire-level. */
  readonly uploads: Map<number, {
    /** The chunks received so far. */
    bytes: Buffer[];
    /** The announced total size in bytes. */
    expected: number;
  }>;
  /** Snapshots taken with `media.capture`, by snapshot id. Wire-level. */
  readonly snapshots: Map<number, Json>;
  /** Every `jobs.start` request (`kind`, `destination`, `quality`, …), newest last. */
  readonly exports: Record<string, Json>[];
  /** Export jobs by job id. Each state query advances a job one step (`queued` → `running` → `completed`; `cancelling` → `cancelled`). Wire-level. */
  readonly jobs: Map<number, MediaJob>;
  /**
   * `openStream`'s transport: a Unix socket (macOS, Linux) or, with `"tcp"`, loopback TCP where the plugin must send the token first (Windows). Set it before the plugin calls `openStream`.
   */
  producerTransport: "unix" | "tcp";
  /** Generated streams (`player.openStream`) by producer id: the fake player end of each frame connection. Wire-level beyond the FakeProducer fields. */
  readonly producers: Map<number, FakeProducer & {
    /** The listening server for the frame connection. */
    server: Server;
    /** The Unix socket path (unused with TCP). */
    path: string;
    /** TCP: the connection sent the right token (always true for Unix). */
    admitted: boolean;
    /** The current start/stop control epoch. */
    epoch: number;
    /** A control waiting for the plugin's acknowledgement, or `null`. */
    pending: Json | null;
    /** Whether the last control was acknowledged. */
    acknowledged: boolean;
    /** Whether the stream is producing (selected and started). */
    active: boolean;
  }>;
  /** Registered source resolvers (`resolvers.add`) by id: their declarations. */
  readonly resolvers: Map<string, Json>;
  /**
   * Resolvers other plugins hold, as `resolvers.add` declares them plus the holder's id: a registration of this plugin that claims one of their extensions (or scheme + host pairs) is refused with `conflict`, which does not fail activation, like the player.
   */
  readonly otherResolvers: {
    /** The manifest id of the plugin holding them (shown in the refusal). */
    owner: string;
    /** File extensions it resolves (a file resolver), lower case, no dot. */
    extensions?: string[];
    /** URL schemes it resolves (a web resolver), with `hosts`. */
    schemes?: string[];
    /** Exact host names it resolves (a web resolver), with `schemes`. */
    hosts?: string[];
  }[];
  /** What `plugin.resolvers.fileTypes` reports: the extensions of this plugin's file resolvers and of TestHost.otherResolvers, sorted, each once. */
  fileTypes(): string[];
  /**
   * Push `resolvers.fileTypes` when TestHost.fileTypes changed: called after this plugin's resolvers come and go; call it yourself after changing TestHost.otherResolvers (another plugin started or stopped).
   */
  updateFileTypes(): void;
  /**
   * File opens waiting for this plugin's file resolver (`extensions`), by request id: the path and how it was opened. Opening a matching path (`player.open`, TestHost.openElsewhere) sends `source.resolveRequest`; the answer selects the stream, fails the open or, once the source changed, is `stale`. Any later source change cancels it (`source.resolveCancel`). Web resolvers are not simulated: emit `source.resolveRequest` yourself.
   */
  readonly resolutions: Map<number, {
    /** The id of this plugin's resolver asked (`resolvers.add` `id`). */
    resolverId: string;
    /** The path being opened, as sent to `resolve`. */
    source: string;
    /** The open asked for a paused start (`player.open(path, { paused })`). */
    paused: boolean;
  }>;
  /**
   * Answers for `dialogs.open` (paths, `null` = cancelled) and
   * `dialogs.confirm` (`{ confirmed, checked }`), consumed in order. A
   * dialog with no queued answer, or with the wrong kind, fails the request
   * (as a lost reply).
   *
   * For `openFile` / `openDirectory` / `saveFile` queue a one-path array;
   * for `openFiles` any number of paths.
   */
  readonly dialogAnswers: (string[] | null | {
    /** The user clicked the confirm button. */
    confirmed: boolean;
    /** The checkbox state. */
    checked: boolean;
  })[];
  /** Every `dialogs.confirm` request (its options), newest last. */
  readonly confirms: Record<string, Json>[];
  /**
   * The main window as the player would show it. Change it with `setMainWindow` (the user resized it, entered fullscreen, closed the picture-in-picture window); `onTop`, `cursorAutoHide` and `pictureInPicture.active` record the plugin's `window.set…` calls. `pictureInPicture.supported: false` stands for Windows and Linux.
   */
  readonly mainWindow: {
    /** Whether the main window is fullscreen. */
    fullscreen: boolean;
    /** The video area in logical points (default 780×609). */
    videoArea: {
      /** Width in logical points. */
      width: number;
      /** Height in logical points. */
      height: number;
    };
    /** The effective `window.setAlwaysOnTop` value. */
    onTop: boolean;
    /** The effective `window.setCursorAutoHide` mode. */
    cursorAutoHide: "fullscreen" | "playing";
    /** Picture-in-picture: `supported` (preset) and `active`. */
    pictureInPicture: {
      /** Set to `false` to simulate Windows or Linux. */
      supported: boolean;
      /** Whether the picture-in-picture window shows the video. */
      active: boolean;
    };
  };
  /**
   * The player's secret store for this plugin: name → value. Preset entries to simulate stored secrets; inject failures with `host.handle("secrets.get", ...)`. Like the player, `secrets.set` of a new name fails `limit` once 256 names are stored.
   */
  readonly secrets: Map<string, string>;
  /** What `plugin.app.system()` reports. */
  systemInfo: WireSystemInfo;
  /** What `plugin.app` reports. Set it before startPlugin: the plugin receives it once at start-up. */
  app: {
    /** The player version. */
    version: string;
    /** The short git hash of the build, `null` when unknown. */
    build: string | null;
    /** Component versions. */
    components: {
      /** libmpv's `mpv-version`. */
      mpv: string | null;
      /** `{ ffmpeg: <version> }`. */
      libav: Record<string, string>;
      /** The Slint version. */
      slint: string;
    };
  };
  /** What `player.chapters()` lists while media is ready. */
  chapters: {
    /** The chapter title, `null` without one. */
    title: string | null;
    /** Start time in seconds. */
    start: number;
  }[];
  /**
   * `plugin.dataDirectory`: a fresh empty temporary directory, removed with the host on `stop()`. `plugin.storage.json` reads and writes real files here. Pass `startPlugin(..., { dataDirectory })` to use another one.
   */
  readonly dataDirectory: string;
  /** The manifest id of the plugin under test (set by startPlugin; `"test.plugin"` by default). */
  manifestId: string;
  constructor();
  /** The `player.setStepSeek` value in effect (default 5). */
  stepSeek: number;
  /** Every `player.step`, newest last. */
  readonly steps: {
    /** `"frame"` or `"keyframe"`. */
    unit: string;
    /** `"backward"` or `"forward"`. */
    direction: string;
  }[];
  /** Every core action run (`host.run`, a core command, a pressed core binding), newest last. */
  readonly coreRuns: string[];
  /**
   * One of the 14 core actions (`play-pause`, `stop`, `seek-forward`, ...) that the test host registers like the player, as `host/<id>`. Throws for an unknown id. `run()` executes it with the player's checks and writes its on-screen text to TestHost.osd.
   */
  coreAction(id: string): FakeCommand;
  /**
   * Replace the host's behaviour for one wire method until
   * TestHost.reset. The handler receives the request parameters and
   * returns the reply (or a promise of it).
   *
   * Throw a HostError to simulate a definite refusal (the plugin's
   * call rejects with that `code`); throw a plain `Error` to simulate a lost
   * reply (the SDK then runs its recovery path). Method names are protocol
   * names, e.g. `"clipboard.writeText"`, `"secrets.get"`,
   * `"system.openPath"`, `"audio.addTrack"`; see TestHost.sent to
   * find the one a call uses.
   * @param method - The wire method name.
   * @param handler - Produces the reply from the request parameters.
   */
  handle(method: string, handler: Handler): void;
  /** Restore the default behaviour of a method replaced with TestHost.handle. */
  reset(method: string): void;
  /**
   * Deliver a host event to the plugin. Like the player, subscription-based events (`source.state`, `playback.backend`, `window.state`, `timeline.changed`, `appearance.changed`) are delivered only when the plugin subscribed (it declared `events` and listens). Most tests use the higher-level helpers (`setSource`, `setMainWindow`, ...) instead.
   * @param event - The wire event name.
   * @param data - The event payload (wire-level shape).
   */
  emit(event: string, data: unknown): void;
  /**
   * Change the source facts and broadcast them, as if the player's state changed (the user paused, playback reached the end, a file finished loading). Any phase other than `empty` also turns on the source capabilities (pause, seek, rate, ...) unless the patch sets them. `phase: "loading"` makes a mounted backdrop effective, like the player.
   * @param patch - Wire-level source fields, e.g. `phase`, `position`, `duration`, `paused`, `audioTracks`.
   */
  setSource(patch: Partial<SourceState>): void;
  /**
   * Simulate the user changing the main window (resizing it, entering or leaving fullscreen, closing the picture-in-picture window) and broadcast it. Like the player, entering fullscreen collapses an attached, visible sidebar (`effective: false`, `reason: "fullscreen"`) and leaving fullscreen docks it again.
   */
  setMainWindow(patch: Partial<{
    fullscreen: boolean;
    videoArea: {
      width: number;
      height: number;
    };
    pictureInPicture: {
      supported: boolean;
      active: boolean;
    };
  }>): void;
  /**
   * The pointer reached the right edge in fullscreen (`true`) or left the popped-out sidebar (`false`): the attached sidebar pops out or collapses (reference §6.3). No effect outside fullscreen, when hidden or floating.
   */
  popSidebar(popped: boolean): void;
  /**
   * Simulate another plugin (or the user) opening a source: a new `sourceId`, then the given phase. Calls the plugin made against the old state now fail with `stale`.
   * @param source - The path or URL.
   * @param phase - The phase to end in (default `"ready"`).
   */
  openElsewhere(source: string, phase?: SourceState["phase"]): void;
  /**
   * Simulate a generated stream failing in the player (its audio device lost, its frame connection broken), like the player: the source fails with `message` (`phase: "error"`) and the producer is retired at once. The stream's `onStop` listeners get a `stream` error with `message`.
   * @param producerId - The producer, from TestHost.producers.
   * @param message - The player's failure text.
   */
  failStream(producerId: number, message: string): void;
  /**
   * Press a binding like the host's table would: panel-focus bindings first when `panel` is true, then global ones; within a scope the earliest registration first (the player's own commands before the plugin's), as the conflict rule orders them. A disabled command lets the key pass to the next command bound to it (SDK 1.5.12, as player 0.4.3): the one it shadowed, then the global scope. The first enabled one runs; `press` resolves after it ran (`"ran"`), or rejects when it is busy. When only disabled commands hold the key, the first one with a `reason` shows the reason on the OSD and eats the key (`"reason"`, see `host.osd`); without a reason the key goes on to the focused control (`"passed"`, nothing runs). Rejects when nothing is bound. Bindings use the reference syntax (`"Space"`, `"Ctrl+O"`, `"Mouse:WheelUp"`), and user overrides in `bindings.overlay` apply.
   * @returns What the key did: `"ran"`, `"reason"` or `"passed"`.
   */
  press(binding: string, options?: {
    panel?: boolean;
  }): Promise<"ran" | "reason" | "passed">;
  /** Bindings declared by more than one command, each as `[binding, winner, ...ignored]` (command ids; core actions as `host/<id>`). Empty when there are none. */
  get conflicts(): string[][];
  /** The binding overlay `plugin.bindings.set` writes (`"<plugin>/<command>"` to inputs; preset it to simulate saved overrides). `press` honours it. */
  readonly bindings: {
    /** `"<plugin>/<command>"` → the user's inputs for it. */
    overlay: Map<string, string[]>;
  };
  /**
   * What `packages.list` reports; `setEnabled`, `uninstall` and `install` update it. `builtin`, `source` and `dataDirectory` are optional here (default `false`, `null`, `null`).
   */
  packages: {
    /** The plugin's manifest id. */
    id: string;
    /** Its version, `null` when unknown. */
    version: string | null;
    /** Where it was loaded from. */
    origin: "installed" | "development";
    /** Its run state. */
    state: "starting" | "running" | "disabled" | "failed" | "stopped";
    /** Why it failed (`state: "failed"`). */
    error: string | null;
    /** Its declared capabilities. */
    capabilities: string[];
    /** The package directory. */
    directory: string;
    /** The version a rollback would restore, `null` without one. */
    previousVersion: string | null;
    /** Shipped with the player: `uninstall` and `install` are `unsupported`. */
```
